title.en: Volume 31 Biographies 1: Empresses and Consorts Part One

proposal.before: her mother was a Shan from Henei, first cousin once removed to Grand Tutor Shan Tao.
proposal.after: her mother was a Shan from Henei, first cousin once removed to Minister over the Masses Shan Tao.
proposal.reason: 司徒 is Minister over the Masses, not Grand Tutor (太傅); literal error: the office is mistranslated.

context.zh: 宣穆張皇后諱春華，河內平皋人也。
context.idiomatic: Empress Zhang Xuanmu, personal name Chunhua, came from Pinggao in Henei commandery.
context.literal: Empress Zhang Xuanmu, taboo name Chunhua, was a native of Pinggao in Henei.

context.zh: 父汪，魏粟邑令；
context.idiomatic: Her father Wang had served as magistrate of Suiyi under Wei;
context.literal: Her father Wang was magistrate of Suiyi in Wei;

context.zh: 母河內山氏，司徒濤之從祖姑也。
context.idiomatic: her mother was a Shan from Henei, first cousin once removed to Grand Tutor Shan Tao.
context.literal: her mother was a Shan of Henei, a paternal grand-aunt by cousinship of Minister of Education Tao.

context.zh: 后少有德行，智識過人，生景帝、文帝、平原王幹、南陽公主。
context.idiomatic: She showed virtue and unusual discernment from girlhood. She was mother to Emperors Jing and Wen, to Prince Sima Gan of Pingyuan, and to the Princess of Nanyang.
context.literal: The empress from youth had virtuous conduct and intelligence surpassing others; she bore Emperor Jing, Emperor Wen, Prince Gan of Pingyuan, and the Princess of Nanyang.

context.zh: 宣帝初辭魏武之命，託以風痹，嘗暴書，遇暴雨，不覺自起收之。
context.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan first refused Cao Cao’s summons, claiming crippling palsy, he once aired books in the sun. A cloudburst came; forgetting his act, he leapt up to rescue them.
context.literal: When Emperor Xuan at first declined Wei Wu’s summons, pleading wind paralysis, he once sunned books; encountering a sudden storm, unthinkingly he rose himself to gather them in.

proposal.before: She died in 247 at fifty-nine and was buried at Gaoyuan mausoleum east of Luoyang; Wei later enfeoffed her posthumously as Lady of Guangping.
proposal.after: She died in 247 at fifty-nine and was buried at Gaoyuan mausoleum at Luoyang; Wei later enfeoffed her posthumously as Lady of Guangping.
proposal.reason: 葬洛陽高原陵 says only that she was buried at Gaoyuan mausoleum, Luoyang; literal error: "east of" is invented.

context.zh: 帝驚而致謝，后乃止。
context.idiomatic: Alarmed, he apologized, and she gave up the attempt.
context.literal: The emperor was alarmed and apologized; the empress then stopped.

context.zh: 帝退而謂人曰：「老物不足惜，慮困我好兒耳！」
context.idiomatic: Privately he muttered, “I care nothing for the hag—I fear only harm to my fine sons.”
context.literal: The emperor withdrew and said to someone: “The old creature is not worth pity—I worry she will distress my good sons!”

context.zh: 魏正始八年崩，時年五十九，葬洛陽高原陵，追贈廣平縣君。
context.idiomatic: She died in 247 at fifty-nine and was buried at Gaoyuan mausoleum east of Luoyang; Wei later enfeoffed her posthumously as Lady of Guangping.
context.literal: She died in Wei’s eighth Zhengshi year, aged fifty-nine, buried at Gaoyuan tumulus in Luoyang, posthumously endowed as Lady of Guangping County.

context.zh: 咸熙元年，追號宣穆妃。
context.idiomatic: In 264 she received the posthumous title Consort Xuanmu.
context.literal: In the first Xianxi year she was posthumously titled Consort Xuanmu.

context.zh: 及武帝受禪，追尊為皇后。
context.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu took the throne, she was raised posthumously to empress.
context.literal: When Emperor Wu received the abdication, she was posthumously honored as empress.

proposal.before: Under Wei Mingdi, Sima Yi commanded the armies while his sons showed ruthless ambition.
proposal.after: Under Wei Mingdi, Sima Yi commanded the armies while his sons all had heroic talent and grand strategic vision.
proposal.reason: 諸子並有雄才大略 praises heroic talent and grand strategy; literal error: "ruthless ambition" inverts the tone.

context.zh: 母曹氏，魏德陽鄉主。
context.idiomatic: her mother was a daughter of the Wei imperial house, titled Village Mistress of Deyang.
context.literal: her mother was a Cao, Village Mistress of Deyang in Wei.

context.zh: 后雅有識度，帝每有所為，必豫籌畫。
context.idiomatic: She was poised and far-sighted; whatever her husband planned, she anticipated and shaped.
context.literal: The empress elegantly had insight and measure; whenever the emperor had something to do, she always planned ahead.

context.zh: 魏明帝世，宣帝居上將之重，諸子並有雄才大略。
context.idiomatic: Under Wei Mingdi, Sima Yi commanded the armies while his sons showed ruthless ambition.
context.literal: In Emperor Ming of Wei’s reign, Emperor Xuan occupied the weight of supreme commander; his sons all had heroic talent and broad strategies.

context.zh: 后知帝非魏之純臣，而后既魏氏之甥，帝深忌之。
context.idiomatic: She knew Sima Yi was no loyal servant of Wei, yet as a Wei princess by birth she herself drew his deepest suspicion.
context.literal: The empress knew the emperor was not a pure minister of Wei, yet the empress was moreover a niece of the Wei clan—deeply the emperor suspected her.

context.zh: 青龍二年，遂以鴆崩，時年二十四，葬峻平陵。
context.idiomatic: In 234 she was poisoned at twenty-four and buried at Junping mausoleum.
context.literal: In the second Qinglong year she then died by poisoned wine, aged twenty-four, buried at Junping tumulus.

proposal.before: She knew Sima Yi was no loyal servant of Wei, yet as a Wei princess by birth she herself drew his deepest suspicion.
proposal.after: She knew Sima Yi was no loyal servant of Wei, yet as a maternal niece of the Wei ruling house she herself drew his deepest suspicion.
proposal.reason: 魏氏之甥 means a sister's child of the Wei (Cao) house; her mother was a Cao. Literal error: "Wei princess by birth" overstates her status.

context.literal: In Emperor Ming of Wei’s reign, Emperor Xuan occupied the weight of supreme commander; his sons all had heroic talent and broad strategies.

context.idiomatic: She knew Sima Yi was no loyal servant of Wei, yet as a Wei princess by birth she herself drew his deepest suspicion.
context.literal: The empress knew the emperor was not a pure minister of Wei, yet the empress was moreover a niece of the Wei clan—deeply the emperor suspected her.

context.idiomatic: In 234 she was poisoned at twenty-four and buried at Junping mausoleum.
context.literal: In the second Qinglong year she then died by poisoned wine, aged twenty-four, buried at Junping tumulus.

context.zh: 武帝登阼，初未追崇，弘訓太后每以為言，泰始二年始加號諡。
context.idiomatic: After Emperor Wu took the throne he left her unhonored until Empress Dowager Yang at Hongxun repeatedly pressed the matter; only in 266 did he grant posthumous rank and epithet.
context.literal: When Emperor Wu ascended the throne, at first he did not posthumously honor her; Empress Dowager Hongxun often spoke of it; only in the second Taishi year did he begin adding title and posthumous name.

proposal.before: her mother was a Cai from Chenliu, daughter of the Han court poet Cai Yong.
proposal.after: her mother was a Cai from Chenliu, daughter of the Han General of the Household of the Left Cai Yong.
proposal.reason: 漢左中郎將邕 gives Cai Yong's office, General of the Household of the Left; literal error: "court poet" replaces the office.

context.zh: 景獻羊皇后諱徽瑜，泰山南城人。
context.idiomatic: Empress Yang Jingxian, personal name Huiyu, came from Nancheng in Taishan commandery.
context.literal: Empress Yang Jingxian, taboo name Huiyu, was a person of Nancheng in Taishan.

context.zh: 父茞，上黨太守；
context.idiomatic: Her father Yang Zhi served as governor of Shangdang;
context.literal: Her father Zhi was governor of Shangdang;

context.zh: 后母陳留蔡氏，漢左中郎將邕之女也。
context.idiomatic: her mother was a Cai from Chenliu, daughter of the Han court poet Cai Yong.
context.literal: the empress’s mother was a Cai of Chenliu, daughter of Han’s Left General of the Household Cai Yong.

context.zh: 后聰敏有才行。
context.idiomatic: She was quick-witted, talented, and principled.
context.literal: The empress was clever, keen, and had talent and conduct.

context.zh: 景懷皇后崩，景帝更娶鎮北將軍濮陽吳質女，見黜，復納后，無子。
context.idiomatic: After Empress Xiahou died, Emperor Jing married Wu Zhi’s daughter, then divorced her, and took Yang Huiyu back; she bore no sons.
context.literal: When Empress Jinghuai died, Emperor Jing further married the daughter of Wu Zhi of Puyang, General Who Guards the North; she was dismissed; he took in the empress again; she had no sons.

proposal.before: After Empress Xiahou died, Emperor Jing married Wu Zhi’s daughter, then divorced her, and took Yang Huiyu back; she bore no sons.
proposal.after: After Empress Xiahou died, Emperor Jing married the daughter of Wu Zhi of Puyang, General Who Guards the North; she was dismissed, and he then married Yang Huiyu; she bore no sons.
proposal.reason: 復納后 means he then married the empress (Yang); she had not been his wife before. Literal error: "took back" invents an earlier marriage and the office 鎮北將軍 was dropped.

context.zh: 后母陳留蔡氏，漢左中郎將邕之女也。
context.idiomatic: her mother was a Cai from Chenliu, daughter of the Han court poet Cai Yong.
context.literal: the empress’s mother was a Cai of Chenliu, daughter of Han’s Left General of the Household Cai Yong.

context.zh: 后聰敏有才行。
context.idiomatic: She was quick-witted, talented, and principled.
context.literal: The empress was clever, keen, and had talent and conduct.

context.zh: 景懷皇后崩，景帝更娶鎮北將軍濮陽吳質女，見黜，復納后，無子。
context.idiomatic: After Empress Xiahou died, Emperor Jing married Wu Zhi’s daughter, then divorced her, and took Yang Huiyu back; she bore no sons.
context.literal: When Empress Jinghuai died, Emperor Jing further married the daughter of Wu Zhi of Puyang, General Who Guards the North; she was dismissed; he took in the empress again; she had no sons.

context.zh: 武帝受禪，居弘訓宮，號弘訓太后。
context.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu assumed the throne she moved to Hongxun Palace as dowager.
context.literal: When Emperor Wu received the abdication, she resided in Hongxun Palace, titled Empress Dowager Hongxun.

context.zh: 泰始九年，追贈蔡氏濟陽縣君，諡曰穆。
context.idiomatic: In 273 her mother was posthumously named Lady of Jiyang with the epithet Mu.
context.literal: In the ninth Taishi year Lady Cai was posthumously endowed as Mistress of Jiyang County, posthumous name Mu.

proposal.before: Because his mother-in-law lacked posthumous honors, Emperor Wu issued in 267 an edict: “Han Wendi raised Empress Dowager Bo’s title; later Han rulers enfeoffed mothers from Pingyuan and Boping—such acts honor parents and widen kinship grace.
proposal.after: Because his mother-in-law lacked posthumous honors, Emperor Wu issued in 267 an edict: “Han Wendi conferred the posthumous title Lingwen; Emperors Wu and Xuan of Han granted the fiefs of Pingyuan and Boping—such acts honor parents and widen kinship grace.
proposal.reason: 靈文 is the posthumous title Han Wendi gave his maternal grandfather, and 武、宣 are Emperors Wu and Xuan of Han; literal error: "Empress Dowager Bo" and "mothers" misidentify the honorees.

context.zh: 后雖處尊位，不忘素業，躬執紡績，器服無文，御浣濯之衣，食不參味。
context.idiomatic: Though dowager, she still spun and wove, wore undyed cloth and laundered robes, and took simple meals without mixed dishes.
context.literal: Although the empress occupied an honored position, she did not forget her plain work; personally she held spinning and weaving; vessels and garments had no pattern; she employed washed clothing; food did not mix flavors.

context.zh: 而敦睦九族，垂心萬物，言必典禮，浸潤不行。
context.idiomatic: She cherished every branch of kin, cared for all living things, spoke only in classical idiom, and never let private bias seep into policy.
context.literal: Yet she treated the nine kindreds warmly, let her heart hang over all things; speech always followed canon and ritual; seeping influence did not proceed.

context.zh: 帝以后母羊氏未崇諡號，泰始三年下詔曰：「昔漢文追崇靈文之號，武、宣有平原、博平之封，咸所以奉尊尊之敬，廣親親之恩也。
context.idiomatic: Because his mother-in-law lacked posthumous honors, Emperor Wu issued in 267 an edict: “Han Wendi raised Empress Dowager Bo’s title; later Han rulers enfeoffed mothers from Pingyuan and Boping—such acts honor parents and widen kinship grace.
context.literal: The emperor because the empress’s mother the Yang clan had not been honored with posthumous title, in the third Taishi year issued an edict saying: “Formerly Han Wen posthumously elevated the title of Lingwen; Wu and Xuan had enfeoffments of Pingyuan and Boping—all were means to serve respect to the honored and widen kindness to kin.

context.zh: 故衛將軍、蘭陵景侯夫人羊氏，含章體順，仁德醇備，內承世冑，出嬪大國，三從之行，率禮無違。
context.idiomatic: Lady Yang, widow of General Wang Su, Marquis Jing of Lanling, bore inward grace and outward modesty, fulfilled every womanly virtue, linked great houses by marriage, and observed the three obediences without fault.
context.literal: Therefore Lady Yang, wife of General Who Guards the Army, Marquis Jing of Lanling, contained pattern and embodied compliance; humane virtue pure and complete; inwardly inheriting generations of lineage, outwardly marrying a great state; in the conduct of the three followings, leading ritual without violation.

context.zh: 仍遭不造，頻喪統嗣，撫育眾胤，克成家道。
context.idiomatic: Though Heaven denied her sons and struck down heirs again and again, she raised the wider family and preserved the household.
context.literal: Yet she encountered ill fortune, repeatedly losing heirs who would succeed, fostering many descendants, able to complete family way.

proposal.before: Still grieving, he issued another edict: “Lady Yang, wife of former Minister Wang Lang and my maternal great-grandmother, together with my maternal uncles and my two aunts on the Zheng and Liu sides, were cherished by successive empresses.
proposal.after: Still grieving, he issued another edict: “Lady Yang, wife of former Minister Wang Lang and my maternal great-grandmother, together with my maternal uncles and my two aunts on the Zheng and Liu sides, were dearly loved by the late empress.
proposal.reason: 先后至愛 means they were the late empress's (Wang Yuanji's) dearest kin; literal error: "successive empresses" misreads 先后.

context.zh: 尚或有聞，顧予孤遺。
context.idiomatic: Perhaps you still may hear—turn once to your forsaken child.
context.literal: Perhaps you still may hear—look upon me, orphaned and left behind.

context.zh: 嗚呼哀哉！
context.idiomatic: Alas for this sorrow!
context.literal: Alas, oh grief!

context.zh: 其後帝追慕不已，復下詔曰：「外曾祖母故司徒王朗夫人楊氏，舅氏尊屬，鄭、劉二從母，先后至愛。
context.idiomatic: Still grieving, he issued another edict: “Lady Yang, wife of former Minister Wang Lang and my maternal great-grandmother, together with my maternal uncles and my two aunts on the Zheng and Liu sides, were cherished by successive empresses.
context.literal: Afterward the emperor’s longing did not cease; he again issued an edict saying: “My maternal great-grandmother, Lady Yang, wife of former Minister of Education Wang Lang, my uncles’ honored kin, and my two maternal aunts of the Zheng and Liu clans were deeply beloved by the late consorts.

context.zh: 每惟聖善，敦睦遺旨，渭陽之感，永懷靡及。
context.idiomatic: Whenever I recall their kindness and the generous instructions they left, the ache of a nephew for his mother’s kin stays with me yet can never be satisfied.
context.literal: Whenever pondering their sacred goodness and generous instructions, the Wei-yang longing—forever cherished yet never attained.

context.zh: 其封楊夫人及從母為鄉君，邑各五百戶。」
context.idiomatic: Let Lady Yang and my maternal aunts each receive the title of village mistress with five hundred taxable households.”
context.literal: Let Lady Yang and the maternal aunts be enfeoffed as village mistresses, five hundred households each.”

proposal.before: Her father Yang Wenzhong [2] is treated in the “Treatise on Outer Kin”;
proposal.after: Her father Yang Wenzong [2] is treated in the “Treatise on Outer Kin”;
proposal.reason: 文宗 is romanized Wenzong; literal error: "Wenzhong" misspells the name.

context.zh: 武元楊皇后
context.idiomatic: Empress Yang the Martial and Primordial
context.literal: Empress Yang Wuyuan

context.zh: 武元楊皇后諱艷，字瓊芝，弘農華陰人也。
context.idiomatic: Empress Yang Wuyuan, personal name Yan, courtesy Qiongzhi, came from Huayin in Hongnong commandery.
context.literal: Empress Yang Wuyuan, taboo name Yan, courtesy name Qiongzhi, was a native of Huayin in Hongnong.

context.zh: 父文宗，見《外戚傳》；
context.idiomatic: Her father Yang Wenzhong [2] is treated in the “Treatise on Outer Kin”;
context.literal: Her father Wenzhong [2]—see the “Treatise on Outer Kin”;

context.zh: 母天水趙氏，早卒。
context.idiomatic: her mother, a Zhao from Tianshui, died while Yang Yan was still young.
context.literal: her mother was a Zhao of Tianshui; she died early.

context.zh: 后依舅家，舅妻仁愛，親乳養后，遣他人乳其子。
context.idiomatic: She grew up in her uncle’s house; his wife nursed Yang Yan herself and hired another wet nurse for her own baby.
context.literal: The empress relied on her uncle’s household; her uncle’s wife was benevolent and loving, personally suckled and raised the empress, and sent another woman to nurse her own child.

proposal.before: Officials asked that, as under Han custom, empress and heir each receive forty bath-fief commanderies, but the emperor refused as non-canonical.
proposal.after: Officials asked that, as under Han custom, empress and heir each receive forty counties as bath-town fiefs, but the emperor refused as non-canonical.
proposal.reason: 食湯沐邑四十縣 is forty counties (縣); literal error: "commanderies" inflates the unit.

context.zh: 甚被寵遇，生毗陵悼王軌、惠帝、秦獻王柬，平陽、新豐、陽平公主。
context.idiomatic: Deeply favored, she bore Prince Gui of Biling, Emperor Hui, Prince Jian of Qin, and the princesses of Pingyang, Xinfeng, and Yangping.
context.literal: She received great favor and bore Prince Gui of Biling, Emperor Hui, Prince Jian of Qin, and the princesses of Pingyang, Xinfeng, and Yangping.

context.zh: 武帝即位，立為皇后。
context.idiomatic: When Sima Yan became emperor, he made her empress.
context.literal: When Emperor Wu took the throne, he established her as empress.

context.zh: 有司奏依漢故事，皇后、太子各食湯沐邑四十縣，而帝以非古典，不許。
context.idiomatic: Officials asked that, as under Han custom, empress and heir each receive forty bath-fief commanderies, but the emperor refused as non-canonical.
context.literal: The offices memorialized that, following Han precedent, the empress and crown prince should each receive forty commanderies as bath-and-maintenance fiefs, but the emperor held this was not ancient practice and did not permit it.

context.zh: 后追懷舅氏之恩，顯官趙俊，納俊兄虞女粲於後宮為夫人。
context.idiomatic: Remembering her uncle’s kindness, she advanced Zhao Jun and took his brother’s daughter Zhao Can into the palace as Honored Lady.
context.literal: The empress recalled her debt to her mother’s clan, promoted Zhao Jun to high office, and brought Jun’s elder brother’s daughter Can into the inner palace as Honored Lady.

context.zh: 帝以皇太子不堪奉大統，密以語后。
context.idiomatic: Believing the crown prince unfit to inherit the realm, he confided as much privately to the empress.
context.literal: The emperor considered the crown prince unable to uphold the great line and secretly spoke of it to the empress.

proposal.before: Jealous by nature, she kept only plain, towering girls and rejected every truly lovely face.
proposal.after: Jealous by nature, she kept only fair-skinned, tall girls and rejected every truly lovely face.
proposal.reason: 潔白長大 means fair-skinned and tall; literal error: "plain" inverts 潔白.

context.zh: 然后盛稱賈后有淑德，又密使太子太傅荀顗進言，上乃聽之。
context.idiomatic: The empress loudly praised Lady Jia’s virtue and secretly had Grand Tutor Xun Yi speak for her, so the emperor yielded.
context.literal: But the empress greatly praised Consort Jia’s virtuous conduct, and also secretly had Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince Xun Yi speak; the sovereign then consented.

context.zh: 泰始中，帝博選良家以充後宮，先下書禁天下嫁娶，使宦者乘使車，給騶騎，馳傳州郡，召充選者使后揀擇。
context.idiomatic: Midway through Taishi he cast a wide net for palace women, banned commoners from marrying, sent eunuchs in official carriages with escorts racing along post roads to every commandery, and had the candidates presented to the empress for her verdict.
context.literal: In the Taishi era the emperor broadly selected good families to fill the rear palace; first he issued a document forbidding marriage in the realm, had eunuchs ride dispatch coaches provided with outriders, gallop relay orders to provinces and commanderies, summon those filling selection and had the empress pick and choose.

context.zh: 后性妒，惟取潔白長大，其端正美麗者並不見留。
context.idiomatic: Jealous by nature, she kept only plain, towering girls and rejected every truly lovely face.
context.literal: The empress was by nature jealous; she only took those fair and tall; those properly beautiful were none of them retained.

context.zh: 時卞藩女有美色，帝掩扇謂后曰：「卞氏女佳。」
context.idiomatic: When Bian Fan’s daughter proved breathtaking, the emperor hid behind his fan and said, “The Bian girl is a jewel.”
context.literal: At the time Bian Fan’s daughter had beautiful looks; the emperor hid behind a fan and said to the empress: “Bian’s daughter is excellent.”

context.zh: 后曰：「藩三世后族，其女不可枉以卑位。」
context.idiomatic: The empress answered, “Three generations of Bians have supplied empresses—such a bride cannot be parked in a petty title.”
context.literal: The empress said: “The Bian clan for three generations has been empress kin—their daughter cannot be slighted with low rank.”

proposal.before: Dying with her head on his knee she said, “Your uncle Yang Jun’s niece combines virtue and beauty—please bring her into the six palaces.”
proposal.after: Dying with her head on his knee she said, “My uncle Yang Jun’s daughter Nanyin combines virtue and beauty—please bring her into the six palaces.”
proposal.reason: 叔父駿女男胤 is "my uncle (Yang) Jun's daughter Nanyin"; literal error: "your uncle" and "niece" reverse the kinship and drop the name.

context.zh: 名家盛族子女，多敗衣瘁貌以避之。
context.idiomatic: Great families dressed their girls in rags and smeared their faces to dodge the draft.
context.literal: Sons and daughters of famous houses and great clans mostly wore tattered clothes and haggard looks to avoid it.

context.zh: 及后有疾，見帝素幸胡夫人，恐後立之，慮太子不安。
context.idiomatic: When she fell ill and saw how he favored Lady Hu, she feared a future empress would threaten her son.
context.literal: When the empress had illness, she saw the emperor always favored Lady Hu and feared she would later be established, worrying for the crown prince’s security.

context.zh: 臨終，枕帝膝曰：「叔父駿女男胤有德色，願陛下以備六宮。」
context.idiomatic: Dying with her head on his knee she said, “Your uncle Yang Jun’s niece combines virtue and beauty—please bring her into the six palaces.”
context.literal: At the end, pillowing on the emperor’s knee she said: “Uncle Yang Jun’s niece has virtue and beauty; I beg Your Majesty to keep her for the six palaces.”

context.zh: 因悲泣，帝流涕許之。
context.idiomatic: She wept; he swore through tears to comply.
context.literal: Thereupon she wept sadly; the emperor promised with flowing tears.

context.zh: 泰始十年，崩於明光殿，絕于帝膝，時年三十七。
context.idiomatic: She died in 274 in Mingguang Hall on his lap, thirty-seven years old.
context.literal: In the tenth Taishi year she died in Mingguang Hall, expired on the emperor’s knee, aged thirty-seven.

proposal.before: She longed to move her parents’ graves but, while court fashion prized austerity, stayed silent until her final hours—this wish moves us still.
proposal.after: She longed to rebury her father and grandfather but, while court fashion prized austerity, stayed silent until her final hours—this wish moves us still.
proposal.reason: 改葬父祖 is reburial of her father and grandfather; literal error: "parents" misidentifies the dead.

context.zh: 詔曰：「皇后逮事先后，常冀能終始永奉宗廟，一旦殂隕，痛悼傷懷。
context.idiomatic: The edict read, “The empress served my late mothers and hoped to honor the shrines to the end; her sudden death tears my heart.
context.literal: An edict said: “The empress served the late consorts in succession, always hoping to be able from beginning to end forever to serve the ancestral temple; suddenly she has fallen—pain and grief wound the heart.

context.zh: 每自以夙喪二親，於家門之情特隆。
context.idiomatic: Orphaned young, she cherished family ties above all else.
context.literal: She often because early lost both parents, toward household affection was especially strong.

context.zh: 又有心欲改葬父祖，以頃者務崇儉約，初不有言，近垂困，說此意，情亦愍之。
context.idiomatic: She longed to move her parents’ graves but, while court fashion prized austerity, stayed silent until her final hours—this wish moves us still.
context.literal: Also she had in mind wishing to reburial father and grandparents; because recent affairs strove to esteem thrift, at first she did not speak; drawing near to death’s agony she stated this intent—the feeling also pities her.

context.zh: 其使領前軍將軍駿等自克改葬之宜，至時，主者供給葬事。
context.idiomatic: Let Forward-General Yang Jun and his colleagues arrange the reburials; officials shall supply whatever is needed when the day comes.
context.literal: Let General of the Van Yang Jun and others themselves determine the propriety of reburial; when the time comes, those in charge shall supply burial affairs.

context.zh: 賜諡母趙氏為縣君，以繼母段氏為鄉君。
context.idiomatic: Honor her mother Lady Zhao as county mistress and her stepmother Lady Duan as village mistress.
context.literal: Posthumously grant Lady Zhao mother title as county mistress, and stepmother Lady Duan as village mistress.

proposal.before: Wang Huang countered: “She conspired with Yang Jun—she cannot share Wu’s temple.
proposal.after: Sima Huang, Prince of Xiapi and Director of the Department of State Affairs, countered: “She conspired with Yang Jun—she cannot share Wu’s temple.
proposal.reason: 下邳王晃 is Sima Huang, Prince (王) of Xiapi; literal error: "Wang Huang" misreads the title 王 as a surname.

context.zh: 中書監張華等以為「太后非得罪于先帝者也，今黨惡所親，[3]為不母于聖世。
context.idiomatic: Zhang Hua argued: “She never wronged Emperor Wu; siding with villains now breaks maternal duty in our era [3].
context.literal: Palace Supervisor Zhang Hua and others held: “The dowager did not offend the late emperor; now she joins wicked kin—she fails motherhood toward this sage age [3].

context.zh: 宜依孝成趙皇后故事，曰武帝皇后，處之離宮，以全貴終之恩。」
context.idiomatic: Treat her like Chengdi’s Zhao—call her Emperor Wu’s consort, lodge her apart, yet grant a decent end.”
context.literal: She should follow Empress Zhao of Emperor Cheng’s precedent—styled Empress of Emperor Wu and housed in a detached palace to preserve honored kindness to the end.”

context.zh: 尚書令、下邳王晃等議曰：「皇太后與駿潛謀，欲危社稷，不可復奉承宗廟，配合先帝。
context.idiomatic: Wang Huang countered: “She conspired with Yang Jun—she cannot share Wu’s temple.
context.literal: Minister Director Prince Kang of Xiapi Huan and others debated: “The empress dowager secretly plotted with Jun to overturn the state—she cannot again serve the temple or pair with the late emperor.

context.zh: 宜貶尊號，廢詣金墉城。」
context.idiomatic: Strip her titles and lock her in Jinyong.”
context.literal: Her honored title should be stripped and she banished to Metal-Walled Fortress.”

context.zh: 于是有司奏：「請從晃等議，廢太后為庶人。
context.idiomatic: Officials petitioned: "We ask to adopt Huang's proposal and depose the dowager as a commoner.
context.literal: Thereupon the offices petitioned: “We ask following Huang’s proposal—depose the dowager as commoner.

proposal.before: In Taining 316 I held the clan office; registers were gone.
proposal.after: In the second year of Taining (324) I held the clan office; registers were gone.
proposal.reason: 太寧二年 is the second year of Taining, AD 324; literal error: "316" is the wrong year.

context.zh: 元后既崩，悼后繼作，至楊駿肆逆，禍延天母。
context.idiomatic: After Yang Yan died came Yang Zhi; Yang Jun’s treason dragged down the queen mother.
context.literal: After the primal empress died, the mourned empress succeeded; when Yang Jun ran riot, calamity reached the Mother of Heaven.

context.zh: 孝懷皇帝追復號諡，豈不以鯀殛禹興，義在不替者乎！
context.idiomatic: Huai restored her honors—as Gun fell but Yu rose, duty survives.
context.literal: Emperor Huai restored her title and epithet—is this not because Gun was executed yet Yu rose—the principle of unbroken obligation?

context.zh: 又太寧二年，臣忝宗正，帝譜泯棄，罔所循按。
context.idiomatic: In Taining 316 I held the clan office; registers were gone.
context.literal: Moreover in the second Taining year I humbly served as Director of the Imperial Clan; imperial genealogies were lost—nothing to consult.

context.zh: 時博諮舊齒，以定昭穆，與故驃騎將軍華恒、尚書荀崧、侍中荀邃因舊譜參論撰次，尊號之重，一無改替。
context.idiomatic: With Hua Heng, Xun Song, and Xun Sui we recomposed charts—her rank stood firm.
context.literal: We broadly queried elders to fix generations and, with former General of Agile Cavalry Hua Heng, Minister Xun Song, Palace Attendant Xun Sui, reviewed old lists to compile order—her lofty title stayed unchanged.

context.zh: 今聖上孝思，祗肅禋祀，詢及群司，將以恢定大禮。
context.idiomatic: Today’s ruler seeks your counsel to fix court ritual.
context.literal: Now our sage sovereign’s filial care solemnly tends sacrifice; he asks all bureaus to settle great ritual.

proposal.before: Pei Yi argued Emperor Ai’s mourned empress kept mourning even after divorce.
proposal.after: The late Vice Director Pei Wei, discussing the precedent of the Mourned Empress, held that mourning for a stepmother continues even after she is cast out.
proposal.reason: 裴頠 is Pei Wei and 悼后 is Empress Wudao; literal error: "Pei Yi" misreads 頠 and "Emperor Ai" is invented.

context.zh: 當時議者欲貶竇后，及后之亡，欲不以禮葬。
context.idiomatic: Critics then sought to shame Dou and withhold burial rites.
context.literal: Debates then wished to demote Dou empress; when she died some wished denial of ritual burial.

context.zh: 和帝以奉事十年，義不可違，臣子之道，務從豐厚，仁明之稱，表于往代。
context.idiomatic: He refused cruelty after ten years’ care—his mercy became legend.
context.literal: He had served her ten years—duty forbade cruelty; ministers pursued lavish burial—his humanity shone for ages.

context.zh: 又見故尚書僕射裴頠議悼后故事，稱繼母雖出，追服無改。
context.idiomatic: Pei Yi argued Emperor Ai’s mourned empress kept mourning even after divorce.
context.literal: I also saw former Minister Director Pei Yi’s opinion on Empress Dao’s case—though a stepmother had departed, mourning obligations stayed unchanged.

context.zh: 是以孝懷皇帝尊崇號諡，還葬峻陵。
context.idiomatic: So Huai restored her posthumous honors at Junling.
context.literal: Therefore Emperor Huai restored honored title and epithet and reburied her at Jun Mausoleum.

context.zh: 此則母子道全，而廢事蕩革也。
context.idiomatic: Kin duty survived though politics had fouled them.
context.literal: Thus mother-son duty stayed whole while violent deeds were swept away.

proposal.before: Yu Yi, Yu Bing, He Chong, Zhuge Hui, Xie Guang, Liu Zhuo, Yin Rong, Feng Huai, and Deng Yi endorsed Tan—Yang Zhi joined Wu’s temple.
proposal.after: Sima Yu, Prince of Kuaiji, Yu Bing, He Chong, Zhuge Hui, Xie Guang, Liu Zhuo, Yin Rong, Feng Huai, and Deng Yi endorsed Tan—Yang Zhi joined Wu’s temple.
proposal.reason: 會稽王昱 is Sima Yu, Prince of Kuaiji; literal error: "Yu Yi" garbles the prince's name.

context.zh: 若以復之為非，則譜諡宜闕，未有位號居正，而偏祠別室者也。
context.idiomatic: if not, her titles should lapse—no legitimate rank receives only a side altar.
context.literal: if restoring her is wrong, then genealogies and epithets should lapse—one cannot hold orthodox rank yet dwell in a side shrine alone.

context.zh: 若以孝懷皇帝私隆母子之道，特為立廟者，此苟崇私情，有虧國典，則國譜帝諱，皆宜除棄，匪徒不得同祀于世祖之廟也。
context.idiomatic: A private shrine for filial piety alone would break precedent and void every register.
context.literal: If Emperor Huai privately enlarged mother-son feeling and built a special temple, that would exalt private affection yet wound state canon—then clan registers and temple names should all be discarded, not merely barred from Wu’s temple.

context.zh: 會稽王昱、中書監庾冰、中書令何充、尚書令諸葛恢、尚書謝廣、光祿勳留擢、丹楊尹殷融、護軍將軍馮懷、散騎常侍鄧逸等咸從潭議，由是太后配食武帝。
context.idiomatic: Yu Yi, Yu Bing, He Chong, Zhuge Hui, Xie Guang, Liu Zhuo, Yin Rong, Feng Huai, and Deng Yi endorsed Tan—Yang Zhi joined Wu’s temple.
context.literal: Prince Hui of Kuaiji Yu, Palace Supervisor Yu Bing, Palace Director He Chong, Minister Director Zhuge Hui, Minister Xie Guang, Superintendent of the Household Liu Zhuo, Intendant of Danyang Yin Rong, Defender-general Feng Huai, and Palace Rider Deng Yi all followed Tan’s opinion; thereby the dowager shared Emperor Wu’s sacrifices.

context.zh: 左貴嬪
context.idiomatic: Lady Zuo of Honorable Rank
context.literal: Honorable Lady Zuo

context.zh: 左貴嬪名芬。
context.idiomatic: Lady Zuo Fen bore that name.
context.literal: The honorable lady Zuo was named Fen.

proposal.before: On that summer day in 274 Jin’s Empress Yang Yan passed—alas!
proposal.after: On the bingyin day of the seventh month, in autumn of the tenth Taishi year (274), Jin’s Empress Yang Yan passed—alas!
proposal.reason: 秋七月丙寅 is the bingyin day of the seventh month in autumn; literal error: "summer day" contradicts 秋 and drops the date.

context.zh: 言及文義，辭對清華，左右侍聽，莫不稱美。
context.idiomatic: Her answers on texts sparkled; every listener praised her grace.
context.literal: When discourse touched literary meaning her replies were lucid and splendid; attendants left and right listened—none failed to praise.

context.zh: 及元楊皇后崩，芬獻誄曰：
context.idiomatic: When Empress Yang Yan died, Zuo Fen offered a lament:
context.literal: When primal Empress Yang Yuan died, Fen presented a dirge, saying:

context.zh: 惟泰始十年秋七月丙寅，晉元皇后楊氏崩，嗚呼哀哉！
context.idiomatic: On that summer day in 274 Jin’s Empress Yang Yan passed—alas!
context.literal: On the bingyin day of autumn in the seventh month of the tenth Taishi year the Jin primal empress Lady Yang died—alas!

context.zh: 昔有莘適殷，姜姒歸周，宣德中闈，徽音永流。
context.idiomatic: Youxin wed Yin; Jiang water wed Zhou—inner chambers rang with virtue.
context.literal: Ancient Youxin married Yin; Jiang Si returned to Zhou—virtue spread within the palace, fair fame forever flows.

context.zh: 樊衛二姬，匡齊翼楚；
context.idiomatic: Fan Ji and Wei Ji uplifted Qi and Chu;
context.literal: The two Ji ladies of Fan and Wei steadied Qi and aided Chu;

proposal.before: Youxin wed Yin; Jiang water wed Zhou—inner chambers rang with virtue.
proposal.after: Youxin wed Yin; Jiang and Si married into Zhou—inner chambers rang with virtue.
proposal.reason: 姜姒 are the Zhou consorts Tai Jiang and Tai Si; literal error: "Jiang water" mistakes the names for a river.

context.zh: 及元楊皇后崩，芬獻誄曰：
context.idiomatic: When Empress Yang Yan died, Zuo Fen offered a lament:
context.literal: When primal Empress Yang Yuan died, Fen presented a dirge, saying:

context.zh: 惟泰始十年秋七月丙寅，晉元皇后楊氏崩，嗚呼哀哉！
context.idiomatic: On that summer day in 274 Jin’s Empress Yang Yan passed—alas!
context.literal: On the bingyin day of autumn in the seventh month of the tenth Taishi year the Jin primal empress Lady Yang died—alas!

context.zh: 昔有莘適殷，姜姒歸周，宣德中闈，徽音永流。
context.idiomatic: Youxin wed Yin; Jiang water wed Zhou—inner chambers rang with virtue.
context.literal: Ancient Youxin married Yin; Jiang Si returned to Zhou—virtue spread within the palace, fair fame forever flows.

context.zh: 樊衛二姬，匡齊翼楚；
context.idiomatic: Fan Ji and Wei Ji uplifted Qi and Chu;
context.literal: The two Ji ladies of Fan and Wei steadied Qi and aided Chu;

context.zh: 馬鄧兩妃，亦毗漢主。
context.idiomatic: Ma and Deng consorts beside Han sovereigns did the same.
context.literal: the two consorts Ma and Deng likewise aided Han sovereigns.

proposal.before: Like Boyu of Zhou I ache—he wore bright robes to delight his kin.
proposal.after: Long ago Boyu, in tender devotion,—he wore bright robes to delight his kin.
proposal.reason: 昔伯瑜之婉孌兮 says "long ago Boyu, so devoted"; literal error: "of Zhou" is invented and "I ache" is not in the line.

context.zh: 日晻曖而無光兮，氣懰慄以洌清。
context.idiomatic: Sunlight fades; the air cuts cold.
context.literal: The sun dims without light; the air bites sharp and clear.

context.zh: 懷愁戚之多感兮，患涕淚之自零。
context.idiomatic: Sorrow crowds my breast; tears fall unbidden.
context.literal: Breast laden with sorrow’s many blows—I fear tears falling of themselves.

context.zh: 昔伯瑜之婉孌兮，每綵衣以娛親。
context.idiomatic: Like Boyu of Zhou I ache—he wore bright robes to delight his kin.
context.literal: Ancient Boyu was tender—he often donned colored robes to cheer his parents.

context.zh: 悼今日之乖隔兮，奄與家為參辰。
context.idiomatic: Today’s cruel divide casts kin as stars that never meet.
context.literal: I mourn today’s cruel separation—suddenly with family I am Orion and Sirius.

context.zh: 豈相去之云遠兮，曾不盈乎數尋。
context.idiomatic: We stand mere feet apart yet cannot bridge the gap.
context.literal: How can they say the distance is far—it does not fill a few yards’ span.

proposal.before: Shaman Wu worked spells; healers He and Que brewed drafts.
proposal.after: Shaman Xian worked spells; healers He and Que brewed drafts.
proposal.reason: 巫咸 is Shaman Xian (咸 is his name); literal error: "Shaman Wu" renders 巫 (shaman) as a name.

context.zh: 云胡不造，于茲禍殃[5]。
context.idiomatic: Why deny Heaven’s favor—why strike her here [5]?
context.literal: Why was fortune not granted—here calamity struck [5]?

context.zh: 寢疾彌留，寤寐不康。
context.idiomatic: She lingered at death’s door—no sleep brought ease.
context.literal: Illness lingered at death’s gate—sleep brought no peace.

context.zh: 巫咸騁術，和鵲奏方。
context.idiomatic: Shaman Wu worked spells; healers He and Que brewed drafts.
context.literal: Wu Xian wielded arts; He and Bian offered prescriptions.

context.zh: 祈禱無應，嘗藥無良。
context.idiomatic: Prayers failed; every draught proved vain.
context.literal: Prayers won no answer; tasted drugs brought no cure.

context.zh: 形神將離，載昏載荒。
context.idiomatic: Body and soul slipped apart—dimming into gloom.
context.literal: Body and spirit parted—darkening, wasting.

proposal.before: Gentle primal queen—she widowed kindness.
proposal.after: Gentle primal queen—she truly spread kindness.
proposal.reason: 實宣慈焉 means she truly spread compassion; literal error: "widowed kindness" is a garbled rendering.

context.zh: 存播令德，沒圖丹青。
context.idiomatic: Alive she spread virtue—dead artists paint her face.
context.literal: Living she spread fair virtue—dead her image paints silks.

context.zh: 先哲之志，以此為榮。
context.idiomatic: Ancient worthies deemed this their glory.
context.literal: Former sages held this—their glory.

context.zh: 溫溫元后，實宣慈焉。
context.idiomatic: Gentle primal queen—she widowed kindness.
context.literal: Gentle primal queen—she truly spread kindness.

context.zh: 撫育群生，恩惠滋焉。
context.idiomatic: She nurtured every life—kindness overflowed.
context.literal: She nurtured all creatures—grace welled forth.

context.zh: 遺愛不已，永見思焉。
context.idiomatic: Her love lingers—memory never fades.
context.literal: Love left behind never ends—forever remembered.

proposal.before: She shot back, “I fear death itself—why fear an emperor?”
proposal.after: She shot back, “I do not fear even death—why should I fear Your Majesty?”
proposal.reason: 死且不畏 means "I do not fear even death"; literal error: "I fear death itself" inverts the meaning.

context.zh: 而芳既入選，下殿號泣。
context.idiomatic: Hu Fang crossed the hall weeping once chosen.
context.literal: When Fang entered selection she descended the hall weeping and crying.

context.zh: 左右止之曰：「陛下聞聲。」
context.idiomatic: Attendants hissed, “The emperor will hear.”
context.literal: Attendants beside her stopped her: “His Majesty will hear your voice.”

context.zh: 芳曰：「死且不畏，何畏陛下！」
context.idiomatic: She shot back, “I fear death itself—why fear an emperor?”
context.literal: Fang said: “I fear not death—why fear His Majesty!”

context.zh: 帝遣洛陽令司馬肇策拜芳為貴嬪。
context.idiomatic: Emperor Wu had Luoyang prefect Sima Zhao invest her with honorable rank.
context.literal: The emperor ordered Luoyang Magistrate Sima Zhao to invest Fang as honorable lady by tally.

context.zh: 帝每有顧問，不飾言辭，率爾而答，進退方雅。
context.idiomatic: Whenever he questioned her she answered straight without flourish—yet comported herself with modest grace.
context.literal: Whenever the emperor questioned her she did not polish phrases—answered plainly yet withdrew with modest grace.

proposal.before: She shot back, “You marched north against Gongsun and west against Zhuge—what else is warlord stock?”
proposal.after: She shot back, “Your house marched north against Gongsun and held off Zhuge in the west—what else is warlord stock?”
proposal.reason: 北伐公孫，西距諸葛 refers to the Sima house's campaigns (Sima Yi), not the emperor himself, and 距 is to resist; literal error: "You marched ... west against" misstates actor and action.

context.zh: 帝嘗與之摴蒱，爭矢，遂傷上指。
context.idiomatic: Playing dice for arrows she wounded his finger.
context.literal: Emperor once played chupu with her; quarreling over arrows they wounded his finger.

context.zh: 帝怒曰：「此固將種也！」
context.idiomatic: He snapped, “That’s pure warrior blood!”
context.literal: Emperor angrily said: “This truly is general stock!”

context.zh: 芳對曰：「北伐公孫，西距諸葛，非將種而何？」
context.idiomatic: She shot back, “You marched north against Gongsun and west against Zhuge—what else is warlord stock?”
context.literal: Fang replied: “North you attacked Gongsun—west you resisted Zhuge—if not general stock, what?”

context.zh: 帝甚有慚色。
context.idiomatic: He flushed with shame.
context.literal: The emperor felt deeply ashamed.

context.zh: 芳生武安公主。
context.idiomatic: She bore Princess Wu’an.
context.literal: Fang bore Princess Wu’an.

proposal.before: On xinmao in early 272 she became crown princess [7].
proposal.after: On the xinmao day of the second month of 272 she became crown princess [7].
proposal.reason: 泰始八年二月辛卯 names the second month; literal error: "early 272" drops the month.

context.zh: 始欲聘后妹午，午年十二，小太子一歲，短小未勝衣。
context.idiomatic: They first chose sister Wu—twelve, petite beside the heir.
context.literal: At first they wished to engage younger sister Wu—Wu twelve years old, one year younger than crown prince, too short for robes.

context.zh: 更娶南風，時年十五，大太子二歲。
context.idiomatic: They wed Nanfeng instead—fifteen, two years his senior.
context.literal: They switched to Nanfeng—then fifteen, two years elder than crown prince.

context.zh: 泰始八年二月辛卯[7]，冊拜太子妃。
context.idiomatic: On xinmao in early 272 she became crown princess [7].
context.literal: Eighth Taishi year second month xinmao [7]—invested crown princess.

context.zh: 妒忌多權詐，太子畏而惑之，嬪御罕有進幸者。
context.idiomatic: Jealous and scheming, she cowed the befuddled prince—other women seldom touched him.
context.literal: Jealous, crafty in intrigue—crown prince feared yet dazed—concubines rarely gained favor.

context.zh: 帝常疑太子不慧，且朝臣和嶠等多以為言，故欲試之。
context.idiomatic: Wu doubted the heir’s wit—He Qiao agreed—so he tested him.
context.literal: Emperor often suspected crown prince dull—and ministers such as He Qiao said same—so wished to test him.

proposal.before: Jia Mo saw danger—planned coup with Pei Yi—Wang Yan backed out.
proposal.after: Jia Mo saw danger—plotted with Pei Wei and Wang Yan to depose her—Wang Yan backed out.
proposal.reason: 裴頠 is Pei Wei and 王衍 was a co-plotter; literal error: "Pei Yi" misreads 頠 and Wang Yan's role is dropped.

context.zh: 繇密欲廢后，賈氏憚之。
context.idiomatic: Sima Yao plotted deposition—Jias feared him.
context.literal: Yao secretly wished depose consort—Jia faction feared him.

context.zh: 及太宰亮、衛瓘等表繇徙帶方，奪楚王中候，后知瑋怨之，乃使帝作密詔令瑋誅瓘、亮，以報宿憾。
context.idiomatic: When Sima Liang and Wei Guan banished Yao and clipped Wei’s guard—she forged orders for Sima Wei to murder Liang and Wei.
context.literal: When Grand Mentor Liang and Wei Guan memorialized to exile Yao to Daifang and strip Prince Chu of central army inspector—consort knew Wei bore grudge—had emperor forge secret edict ordering Wei to kill Guan and Liang—settling old hatred.

context.zh: 模知后凶暴，恐禍及己，乃與裴頠、王衍謀廢之，衍悔而謀寢。
context.idiomatic: Jia Mo saw danger—planned coup with Pei Yi—Wang Yan backed out.
context.literal: Mo knew consort fierce—feared disaster reaching himself—with Pei Yi and Wang Yan plotted deposition—Yan repented—plot slept.

context.zh: 后遂荒淫放恣，與太醫令程據等亂彰內外。
context.idiomatic: She ran riot with physician Cheng Ju.
context.literal: Consort then wanton and dissolute—with Imperial Physician Cheng Ju and others licentious noise inner and outer.

context.zh: 洛南有盜尉部小吏，端麗美容止，既給冢役，忽有非常衣服，眾咸疑其竊盜，尉嫌而辯之。
context.idiomatic: A pretty clerk toiling tombs wore silk—suspected theft.
context.literal: South of Luo petty clerk of thief corps—handsome bearing—assigned tomb labor yet wore extraordinary clothes—all suspected theft—captain interrogated.

proposal.before: Ill diviners forbade “Guangcheng”—she became Princess Yicheng.
proposal.after: Ill diviners forbade “Guangcheng”—her fief was changed to Yicheng.
proposal.reason: 改封宜城 means her enfeoffment was changed to Lady of Yicheng; literal error: "Princess" invents a title she did not hold.
