proposals.reason: 裴頠 is Pei Wei and 王衍 was a co-plotter; literal error: "Pei Yi" misreads 頠 and Wang Yan's role is dropped.

proposals.before: Ill diviners forbade “Guangcheng”—she became Princess Yicheng.
proposals.after: Ill diviners forbade “Guangcheng”—her fief was changed to Yicheng.
proposals.reason: 改封宜城 means her enfeoffment was changed to Lady of Yicheng; literal error: "Princess" invents a title she did not hold.

proposals.before: Minhuai nursed her mother—deferential.
proposals.after: The empress spent more than ten days away tending her sick mother. The crown prince often visited the Yicheng residence with physicians, behaving respectfully and observing every courtesy.
proposals.reason: Corrects the actor: the empress tended her sick mother; restores the crown prince’s visits, physicians, duration and respectful observance.

proposals.before: Jiong hated her mother—Lun used him.
proposals.after: The empress had fallen out with Jiong's mother, which was why Lun sent him.
proposals.reason: Corrects the relationship: the empress had a quarrel with Jiong’s mother; restores why Lun sent Jiong.

proposals.before: May Your Majesty consult further with the Grand Tutor in depth; do not let near and far grow doubtful and draw reproach from all under Heaven."
proposals.after: May Your Majesty consult further with the Grand Steward in depth; do not let near and far grow doubtful and draw reproach from all under Heaven."
proposals.reason: 太宰 is Grand Steward (Sima Yong); literal error: "Grand Tutor" mistranslates the office.

proposals.before: Liu Yao made her consort.
proposals.after: Liu Yao usurped the throne and made her empress.
proposals.reason: 僭位，以為皇后 means he usurped the throne and made her empress; literal error: "consort" understates 皇后 and the usurpation is dropped.

proposals.before: Wu sent her to tutor him in bed—she conceived.
proposals.after: Wu sent her to the Eastern Palace to attend him in bed—she conceived.
proposals.reason: 遣往東宮侍寢 means sent to serve in his bedchamber; literal error: "tutor" is not in the text.

proposals.before: Consort attended illness ten-plus days—crown prince often visited Yicheng mansion—brought physicians—obedient exhaustive ritual.
proposals.after: The empress went out to tend her mother during her illness for more than ten days. The crown prince often visited the Yicheng residence, bringing physicians in and out and respectfully observing every propriety.
proposals.reason: Corrects the actor: the empress tended her sick mother; restores the crown prince’s visits, physicians, duration and respectful observance.

proposals.before: Consort with Jiong’s mother bore grudge—therefore Lun sent him.
proposals.after: The empress had a quarrel with Jiong's mother, so Lun sent him.
proposals.reason: Corrects the relationship: the empress had a quarrel with Jiong’s mother; restores why Lun sent Jiong.

proposals.before: Zhao Can, Jia Wu, Han Shou, Dong Meng executed.
proposals.after: Zhao Can, Jia Wu, Han Shou, Dong Meng and the others were all executed.
proposals.reason: Restores all four named individuals, the others and explicit execution; removes unsupported compression that they died with the empress.

proposals.before: Her cabal died with her.
proposals.after: Zhao Can, Jia Wu, Han Shou, Dong Meng and the others were all executed.
proposals.reason: Restores all four named individuals, the others and explicit execution; removes unsupported compression that they died with the empress.

sentences.zh: 宣穆張皇后諱春華，河內平皋人也。

translations.literal: Empress Zhang Xuanmu, taboo name Chunhua, was a native of Pinggao in Henei.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhang Xuanmu, personal name Chunhua, came from Pinggao in Henei commandery.

sentences.zh: 父汪，魏粟邑令；

translations.literal: Her father Wang was magistrate of Suiyi in Wei;
translations.idiomatic: Her father Wang had served as magistrate of Suiyi under Wei;

sentences.zh: 母河內山氏，司徒濤之從祖姑也。

translations.literal: her mother was a Shan of Henei, a paternal grand-aunt by cousinship of Minister of Education Tao.
translations.idiomatic: her mother was a Shan from Henei, first cousin once removed to Grand Tutor Shan Tao.

sentences.zh: 后少有德行，智識過人，生景帝、文帝、平原王幹、南陽公主。

translations.literal: The empress from youth had virtuous conduct and intelligence surpassing others; she bore Emperor Jing, Emperor Wen, Prince Gan of Pingyuan, and the Princess of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: She showed virtue and unusual discernment from girlhood. She was mother to Emperors Jing and Wen, to Prince Sima Gan of Pingyuan, and to the Princess of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 魏正始八年崩，時年五十九，葬洛陽高原陵，追贈廣平縣君。

translations.literal: She died in Wei’s eighth Zhengshi year, aged fifty-nine, buried at Gaoyuan tumulus in Luoyang, posthumously endowed as Lady of Guangping County.
translations.idiomatic: She died in 247 at fifty-nine and was buried at Gaoyuan mausoleum east of Luoyang; Wei later enfeoffed her posthumously as Lady of Guangping.

sentences.zh: 咸熙元年，追號宣穆妃。

translations.literal: In the first Xianxi year she was posthumously titled Consort Xuanmu.
translations.idiomatic: In 264 she received the posthumous title Consort Xuanmu.

sentences.zh: 及武帝受禪，追尊為皇后。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu received the abdication, she was posthumously honored as empress.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu took the throne, she was raised posthumously to empress.

sentences.zh: 后雅有識度，帝每有所為，必豫籌畫。

translations.literal: The empress elegantly had insight and measure; whenever the emperor had something to do, she always planned ahead.
translations.idiomatic: She was poised and far-sighted; whatever her husband planned, she anticipated and shaped.

sentences.zh: 魏明帝世，宣帝居上將之重，諸子並有雄才大略。

translations.literal: In Emperor Ming of Wei’s reign, Emperor Xuan occupied the weight of supreme commander; his sons all had heroic talent and broad strategies.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wei Mingdi, Sima Yi commanded the armies while his sons showed ruthless ambition.

sentences.zh: 后知帝非魏之純臣，而后既魏氏之甥，帝深忌之。

translations.literal: The empress knew the emperor was not a pure minister of Wei, yet the empress was moreover a niece of the Wei clan—deeply the emperor suspected her.
translations.idiomatic: She knew Sima Yi was no loyal servant of Wei, yet as a Wei princess by birth she herself drew his deepest suspicion.

sentences.zh: 青龍二年，遂以鴆崩，時年二十四，葬峻平陵。

translations.literal: In the second Qinglong year she then died by poisoned wine, aged twenty-four, buried at Junping tumulus.
translations.idiomatic: In 234 she was poisoned at twenty-four and buried at Junping mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 武帝登阼，初未追崇，弘訓太后每以為言，泰始二年始加號諡。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu ascended the throne, at first he did not posthumously honor her; Empress Dowager Hongxun often spoke of it; only in the second Taishi year did he begin adding title and posthumous name.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wu took the throne he left her unhonored until Empress Dowager Yang at Hongxun repeatedly pressed the matter; only in 266 did he grant posthumous rank and epithet.

sentences.zh: 后無男，生五女。

translations.literal: The empress had no sons; she bore five daughters.
translations.idiomatic: She had no sons but five daughters.

sentences.zh: 景獻羊皇后諱徽瑜，泰山南城人。

translations.literal: Empress Yang Jingxian, taboo name Huiyu, was a person of Nancheng in Taishan.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Yang Jingxian, personal name Huiyu, came from Nancheng in Taishan commandery.

sentences.zh: 父茞，上黨太守；

translations.literal: Her father Zhi was governor of Shangdang;
translations.idiomatic: Her father Yang Zhi served as governor of Shangdang;

sentences.zh: 后母陳留蔡氏，漢左中郎將邕之女也。

translations.literal: the empress’s mother was a Cai of Chenliu, daughter of Han’s Left General of the Household Cai Yong.
translations.idiomatic: her mother was a Cai from Chenliu, daughter of the Han court poet Cai Yong.

sentences.zh: 后聰敏有才行。

translations.literal: The empress was clever, keen, and had talent and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: She was quick-witted, talented, and principled.

sentences.zh: 景懷皇后崩，景帝更娶鎮北將軍濮陽吳質女，見黜，復納后，無子。

translations.literal: When Empress Jinghuai died, Emperor Jing further married the daughter of Wu Zhi of Puyang, General Who Guards the North; she was dismissed; he took in the empress again; she had no sons.
translations.idiomatic: After Empress Xiahou died, Emperor Jing married Wu Zhi’s daughter, then divorced her, and took Yang Huiyu back; she bore no sons.

sentences.zh: 武帝受禪，居弘訓宮，號弘訓太后。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu received the abdication, she resided in Hongxun Palace, titled Empress Dowager Hongxun.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu assumed the throne she moved to Hongxun Palace as dowager.

sentences.zh: 泰始九年，追贈蔡氏濟陽縣君，諡曰穆。

translations.literal: In the ninth Taishi year Lady Cai was posthumously endowed as Mistress of Jiyang County, posthumous name Mu.
translations.idiomatic: In 273 her mother was posthumously named Lady of Jiyang with the epithet Mu.

sentences.zh: 咸寧四年，太后崩，時年六十五，祔葬峻平陵。

translations.literal: In the fourth Xianning year the empress dowager died, aged sixty-five, buried by accompaniment at Junping tumulus.
translations.idiomatic: She died in 278 at sixty-five and was interred beside Emperor Jing at Junping.

sentences.zh: 帝以后母羊氏未崇諡號，泰始三年下詔曰：「昔漢文追崇靈文之號，武、宣有平原、博平之封，咸所以奉尊尊之敬，廣親親之恩也。

translations.literal: The emperor because the empress’s mother the Yang clan had not been honored with posthumous title, in the third Taishi year issued an edict saying: “Formerly Han Wen posthumously elevated the title of Lingwen; Wu and Xuan had enfeoffments of Pingyuan and Boping—all were means to serve respect to the honored and widen kindness to kin.
translations.idiomatic: Because his mother-in-law lacked posthumous honors, Emperor Wu issued in 267 an edict: “Han Wendi raised Empress Dowager Bo’s title; later Han rulers enfeoffed mothers from Pingyuan and Boping—such acts honor parents and widen kinship grace.

sentences.zh: 故衛將軍、蘭陵景侯夫人羊氏，含章體順，仁德醇備，內承世冑，出嬪大國，三從之行，率禮無違。

translations.literal: Therefore Lady Yang, wife of General Who Guards the Army, Marquis Jing of Lanling, contained pattern and embodied compliance; humane virtue pure and complete; inwardly inheriting generations of lineage, outwardly marrying a great state; in the conduct of the three followings, leading ritual without violation.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yang, widow of General Wang Su, Marquis Jing of Lanling, bore inward grace and outward modesty, fulfilled every womanly virtue, linked great houses by marriage, and observed the three obediences without fault.

sentences.zh: 仍遭不造，頻喪統嗣，撫育眾胤，克成家道。

translations.literal: Yet she encountered ill fortune, repeatedly losing heirs who would succeed, fostering many descendants, able to complete family way.
translations.idiomatic: Though Heaven denied her sons and struck down heirs again and again, she raised the wider family and preserved the household.

sentences.zh: 母儀之教，光于邦族，誕啟聖明，祚流萬國。

translations.literal: Motherly model instruction shone on state and clan; she broadly opened sagely brightness; fortune flowed to myriad states.
translations.idiomatic: Her maternal example illuminated kin and state, opened the way for the sage-sovereign, and spread blessing across every realm.

sentences.zh: 而早世殂隕，不遇休寵。

translations.literal: Yet she died young and fell, not encountering fine favor.
translations.idiomatic: Yet she died young before receiving such honors.

sentences.zh: 皇太后孝思蒸蒸，永慕罔極。

translations.literal: The empress dowager’s filial thoughts steam upward; forever longing without limit.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager mourns her mother with boundless filial love.

sentences.zh: 朕感存遺訓，追遠傷懷。

translations.literal: I am moved to preserve surviving instructions; tracing the distant, injuring the breast.
translations.idiomatic: Remembering her teaching, I ache when paying tribute to the past.

sentences.zh: 其封夫人為縣君，依德紀諡，主者詳如舊典。」

translations.literal: Let the lady be enfeoffed as county mistress; according to virtue record posthumous name; those in charge detail according to old canons.”
translations.idiomatic: Enfeoff her as a county mistress, grant an epithet suited to her virtue, and let the ministry follow precedent.”

sentences.zh: 於是使使持節謁者何融追諡為平陽靖君。

translations.literal: Thereupon envoy bearing staff and insignia, Yeoman He Rong posthumously titled her Pingyang Lady Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Envoy He Rong was therefore dispatched with tally and staff to confer posthumously the title Lady Jing of Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 其後帝追慕不已，復下詔曰：「外曾祖母故司徒王朗夫人楊氏，舅氏尊屬，鄭、劉二從母，先后至愛。

translations.literal: Afterward the emperor’s longing did not cease; he again issued an edict saying: “My maternal great-grandmother, Lady Yang, wife of former Minister of Education Wang Lang, my uncles’ honored kin, and my two maternal aunts of the Zheng and Liu clans were deeply beloved by the late consorts.
translations.idiomatic: Still grieving, he issued another edict: “Lady Yang, wife of former Minister Wang Lang and my maternal great-grandmother, together with my maternal uncles and my two aunts on the Zheng and Liu sides, were cherished by successive empresses.

sentences.zh: 每惟聖善，敦睦遺旨，渭陽之感，永懷靡及。

translations.literal: Whenever pondering their sacred goodness and generous instructions, the Wei-yang longing—forever cherished yet never attained.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever I recall their kindness and the generous instructions they left, the ache of a nephew for his mother’s kin stays with me yet can never be satisfied.

sentences.zh: 其封楊夫人及從母為鄉君，邑各五百戶。」

translations.literal: Let Lady Yang and the maternal aunts be enfeoffed as village mistresses, five hundred households each.”
translations.idiomatic: Let Lady Yang and my maternal aunts each receive the title of village mistress with five hundred taxable households.”

sentences.zh: 太康七年，追贈繼祖母夏侯氏為滎陽鄉君。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Taikang, his step-grandmother Lady Xiahou was posthumously endowed as village mistress of Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: In 286 he posthumously named his step-grandmother Lady Xiahou village mistress of Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 武元楊皇后諱艷，字瓊芝，弘農華陰人也。

translations.literal: Empress Yang Wuyuan, taboo name Yan, courtesy name Qiongzhi, was a native of Huayin in Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Yang Wuyuan, personal name Yan, courtesy Qiongzhi, came from Huayin in Hongnong commandery.

sentences.zh: 父文宗，見《外戚傳》；

translations.literal: Her father Wenzhong [2]—see the “Treatise on Outer Kin”;
translations.idiomatic: Her father Yang Wenzhong [2] is treated in the “Treatise on Outer Kin”;

sentences.zh: 母天水趙氏，早卒。

translations.literal: her mother was a Zhao of Tianshui; she died early.
translations.idiomatic: her mother, a Zhao from Tianshui, died while Yang Yan was still young.

sentences.zh: 后依舅家，舅妻仁愛，親乳養后，遣他人乳其子。

translations.literal: The empress relied on her uncle’s household; her uncle’s wife was benevolent and loving, personally suckled and raised the empress, and sent another woman to nurse her own child.
translations.idiomatic: She grew up in her uncle’s house; his wife nursed Yang Yan herself and hired another wet nurse for her own baby.

sentences.zh: 及長，又隨後母段氏，依其家。

translations.literal: When grown, she again followed her stepmother Lady Duan and relied on that household.
translations.idiomatic: Later she lived under her stepmother Lady Duan’s roof.

sentences.zh: 后少聰慧，善書，姿質美麗，閑於女工。

translations.literal: The empress was clever from youth, skilled at calligraphy, beautiful in bearing, and adept at women’s crafts.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood she was bright and graceful, wrote well, was strikingly beautiful, and excelled at needlework.

sentences.zh: 有善相者嘗相后，當極貴，文帝聞而為世子聘焉。

translations.literal: A skilled physiognomist once read the empress’s features and said she would reach supreme honor; Emperor Wen heard of it and betrothed her to the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: A physiognomist predicted she would rise to the highest rank, and when Emperor Wen heard this he betrothed her to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 甚被寵遇，生毗陵悼王軌、惠帝、秦獻王柬，平陽、新豐、陽平公主。

translations.literal: She received great favor and bore Prince Gui of Biling, Emperor Hui, Prince Jian of Qin, and the princesses of Pingyang, Xinfeng, and Yangping.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply favored, she bore Prince Gui of Biling, Emperor Hui, Prince Jian of Qin, and the princesses of Pingyang, Xinfeng, and Yangping.

sentences.zh: 武帝即位，立為皇后。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu took the throne, he established her as empress.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Yan became emperor, he made her empress.

sentences.zh: 有司奏依漢故事，皇后、太子各食湯沐邑四十縣，而帝以非古典，不許。

translations.literal: The offices memorialized that, following Han precedent, the empress and crown prince should each receive forty commanderies as bath-and-maintenance fiefs, but the emperor held this was not ancient practice and did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Officials asked that, as under Han custom, empress and heir each receive forty bath-fief commanderies, but the emperor refused as non-canonical.

sentences.zh: 后追懷舅氏之恩，顯官趙俊，納俊兄虞女粲於後宮為夫人。

translations.literal: The empress recalled her debt to her mother’s clan, promoted Zhao Jun to high office, and brought Jun’s elder brother’s daughter Can into the inner palace as Honored Lady.
translations.idiomatic: Remembering her uncle’s kindness, she advanced Zhao Jun and took his brother’s daughter Zhao Can into the palace as Honored Lady.

sentences.zh: 帝以皇太子不堪奉大統，密以語后。

translations.literal: The emperor considered the crown prince unable to uphold the great line and secretly spoke of it to the empress.
translations.idiomatic: Believing the crown prince unfit to inherit the realm, he confided as much privately to the empress.

sentences.zh: 后曰：「立嫡以長不以賢，豈可動乎？」

translations.literal: The empress said: “Establishing the heir depends on seniority among legitimate sons, not on talent—how can that be altered?”
translations.idiomatic: She replied, “The eldest legitimate son succeeds regardless of talent—how can we undo that?”

sentences.zh: 初，賈充妻郭氏使賂后，求以女為太子妃。

translations.literal: At first Jia Chong’s wife Lady Guo sent bribes to the empress, seeking to make her daughter crown princess.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Jia Chong’s wife Lady Guo had bribed her to secure her daughter as crown princess.

sentences.zh: 及議太子婚，帝欲娶衛瓘女。

translations.literal: When discussing the crown prince’s marriage, the emperor wished to take Wei Guan’s daughter.
translations.idiomatic: When the heir’s marriage came under debate, the emperor favored Wei Guan’s daughter.

sentences.zh: 然后盛稱賈后有淑德，又密使太子太傅荀顗進言，上乃聽之。

translations.literal: But the empress greatly praised Consort Jia’s virtuous conduct, and also secretly had Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince Xun Yi speak; the sovereign then consented.
translations.idiomatic: The empress loudly praised Lady Jia’s virtue and secretly had Grand Tutor Xun Yi speak for her, so the emperor yielded.

sentences.zh: 泰始中，帝博選良家以充後宮，先下書禁天下嫁娶，使宦者乘使車，給騶騎，馳傳州郡，召充選者使后揀擇。

translations.literal: In the Taishi era the emperor broadly selected good families to fill the rear palace; first he issued a document forbidding marriage in the realm, had eunuchs ride dispatch coaches provided with outriders, gallop relay orders to provinces and commanderies, summon those filling selection and had the empress pick and choose.
translations.idiomatic: Midway through Taishi he cast a wide net for palace women, banned commoners from marrying, sent eunuchs in official carriages with escorts racing along post roads to every commandery, and had the candidates presented to the empress for her verdict.

sentences.zh: 后性妒，惟取潔白長大，其端正美麗者並不見留。

translations.literal: The empress was by nature jealous; she only took those fair and tall; those properly beautiful were none of them retained.
translations.idiomatic: Jealous by nature, she kept only plain, towering girls and rejected every truly lovely face.

sentences.zh: 時卞藩女有美色，帝掩扇謂后曰：「卞氏女佳。」

translations.literal: At the time Bian Fan’s daughter had beautiful looks; the emperor hid behind a fan and said to the empress: “Bian’s daughter is excellent.”
translations.idiomatic: When Bian Fan’s daughter proved breathtaking, the emperor hid behind his fan and said, “The Bian girl is a jewel.”

sentences.zh: 后曰：「藩三世后族，其女不可枉以卑位。」

translations.literal: The empress said: “The Bian clan for three generations has been empress kin—their daughter cannot be slighted with low rank.”
translations.idiomatic: The empress answered, “Three generations of Bians have supplied empresses—such a bride cannot be parked in a petty title.”

sentences.zh: 帝乃止。

translations.literal: The emperor then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 司徒李胤、鎮軍大將軍胡奮、廷尉諸葛沖、太僕臧權、侍中馮蓀、秘書郎左思及世族子女並充三夫人九嬪之列。

translations.literal: Minister of Education Li Yin, General Who Guards the Army Hu Fen, Commandant of Justice Zhuge Chong, Grand Coachman Zang Quan, Palace Attendant Feng Sun, Secretary Court Gentleman Zuo Si, and daughters of eminent clans together filled the ranks of three ladies and nine bin.
translations.idiomatic: The daughters of Li Yin, Hu Fen, Zhuge Chong, Zang Quan, Feng Sun, Zuo Si, and other great houses were placed among the Three Ladies and the Nine Concubines.

sentences.zh: 司、冀、兗、豫四州二千石將吏家，補良人以下。

translations.literal: Families of two-thousand-shi commandery officials in Si, Ji, Yan, and Yu four prefectures supplied ranks below liangren.
translations.idiomatic: From Si, Ji, Yan, and Yu the daughters of prefects and local officers filled the ranks below Good Woman.

sentences.zh: 名家盛族子女，多敗衣瘁貌以避之。

translations.literal: Sons and daughters of famous houses and great clans mostly wore tattered clothes and haggard looks to avoid it.
translations.idiomatic: Great families dressed their girls in rags and smeared their faces to dodge the draft.

sentences.zh: 及后有疾，見帝素幸胡夫人，恐後立之，慮太子不安。

translations.literal: When the empress had illness, she saw the emperor always favored Lady Hu and feared she would later be established, worrying for the crown prince’s security.
translations.idiomatic: When she fell ill and saw how he favored Lady Hu, she feared a future empress would threaten her son.

sentences.zh: 臨終，枕帝膝曰：「叔父駿女男胤有德色，願陛下以備六宮。」

translations.literal: At the end, pillowing on the emperor’s knee she said: “Uncle Yang Jun’s niece has virtue and beauty; I beg Your Majesty to keep her for the six palaces.”
translations.idiomatic: Dying with her head on his knee she said, “Your uncle Yang Jun’s niece combines virtue and beauty—please bring her into the six palaces.”

sentences.zh: 因悲泣，帝流涕許之。

translations.literal: Thereupon she wept sadly; the emperor promised with flowing tears.
translations.idiomatic: She wept; he swore through tears to comply.

sentences.zh: 泰始十年，崩於明光殿，絕于帝膝，時年三十七。

translations.literal: In the tenth Taishi year she died in Mingguang Hall, expired on the emperor’s knee, aged thirty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: She died in 274 in Mingguang Hall on his lap, thirty-seven years old.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「皇后逮事先后，常冀能終始永奉宗廟，一旦殂隕，痛悼傷懷。

translations.literal: An edict said: “The empress served the late consorts in succession, always hoping to be able from beginning to end forever to serve the ancestral temple; suddenly she has fallen—pain and grief wound the heart.
translations.idiomatic: The edict read, “The empress served my late mothers and hoped to honor the shrines to the end; her sudden death tears my heart.

sentences.zh: 每自以夙喪二親，於家門之情特隆。

translations.literal: She often because early lost both parents, toward household affection was especially strong.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, she cherished family ties above all else.

sentences.zh: 又有心欲改葬父祖，以頃者務崇儉約，初不有言，近垂困，說此意，情亦愍之。

translations.literal: Also she had in mind wishing to reburial father and grandparents; because recent affairs strove to esteem thrift, at first she did not speak; drawing near to death’s agony she stated this intent—the feeling also pities her.
translations.idiomatic: She longed to move her parents’ graves but, while court fashion prized austerity, stayed silent until her final hours—this wish moves us still.

sentences.zh: 其使領前軍將軍駿等自克改葬之宜，至時，主者供給葬事。

translations.literal: Let General of the Van Yang Jun and others themselves determine the propriety of reburial; when the time comes, those in charge shall supply burial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Let Forward-General Yang Jun and his colleagues arrange the reburials; officials shall supply whatever is needed when the day comes.

sentences.zh: 賜諡母趙氏為縣君，以繼母段氏為鄉君。

translations.literal: Posthumously grant Lady Zhao mother title as county mistress, and stepmother Lady Duan as village mistress.
translations.idiomatic: Honor her mother Lady Zhao as county mistress and her stepmother Lady Duan as village mistress.

sentences.zh: 傳不云乎，『慎終追遠，民德歸厚』。

translations.literal: Does not the tradition say, ‘Being careful in one’s end and remembering the remote makes the people’s virtue thick’?
translations.idiomatic: Has not the classic said, ‘Care for the dead and honor the past, and the people grow in virtue’?

sentences.zh: 且使亡者有知，尚或嘉之。」

translations.literal: Moreover, if the dead have knowledge, perhaps they will approve.”
translations.idiomatic: Should the dead still know anything of us, they may rejoice in this kindness.”

sentences.zh: 駿既死，詔使後軍將軍荀悝送后于永寧宮。

translations.literal: After Jun died, an edict ordered Rear-General Xun Kui to escort the empress to Yongning Palace.
translations.idiomatic: After Yang Jun fell, Rear-General Xun Kui was ordered to move her to Yongning Palace.

sentences.zh: 特全后母高都君龐氏之命，聽就后居止。

translations.literal: Her mother Lady Pang of Gaodu Commandery was specially spared and allowed to stay with the dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother Lady Pang was spared and permitted to live with her.

sentences.zh: 賈后諷群公有司奏曰：「皇太后陰漸姦謀，圖危社稷，飛箭繫書，要募將士，同惡相濟，自絕于天。

translations.literal: Empress Jia prompted assembled dukes and offices to memorialize: “The empress dowager secretly carried treason, plotted against the altars, flew arrows with letters tied, summoned soldiers—wicked men aided her and she cut herself off from Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Jia’s faction petitioned: “The dowager schemed treason, imperiled the state, shot letters beyond the walls, and recruited troops—criminals helped her and Heaven abandoned her.

sentences.zh: 魯侯絕文姜，春秋所許，蓋以奉順祖宗，任至公於天下。

translations.literal: Duke Lu cut off Wen Jiang—the Spring and Autumn approves—because one must honor ancestors and hold utmost fairness toward the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Lu cut ties with Wen Jiang, which the Annals condone, to serve ancestors and justice.

sentences.zh: 陛下雖懷無已之情，臣下不敢奉詔。

translations.literal: Although Your Majesty harbors endless feeling, your servants dare not obey the edict.
translations.idiomatic: We know your grief, sire, yet we cannot sanction mercy.

sentences.zh: 可宣敕王公于朝堂會議。」

translations.literal: Let an order proclaim that kings and dukes convene in the court hall to deliberate.”
translations.idiomatic: Summon princes and ministers to the outer court for debate.”

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「此大事，更詳之。」

translations.literal: An edict said: “This is a great matter—consider it again.”
translations.idiomatic: The throne replied, “Weighty—deliberate further.”

sentences.zh: 有司又奏：「駿藉外戚之資，居冢宰之任，陛下既居諒闇，委以重權，至乃陰圖凶逆，布樹私黨。

translations.literal: The offices again memorialized: “Jun relied on affinal backing and held prime minister’s charge; while Your Majesty mourned in the dark palace he received heavy trust, yet secretly plotted treason and planted private partisans.
translations.idiomatic: They answered: “Yang Jun used kinship to seize power; while you mourned he plotted rebellion and packed offices with clients.

sentences.zh: 皇太后內為脣齒，協同逆謀，禍釁既彰，背捍詔命，阻兵負眾，血刃宮省，而復流書募眾，以獎凶黨，上背祖宗之靈，下絕億兆之望。

translations.literal: The empress dowager was his lip and tooth within; she joined the wicked plot. Once the stench showed, she defied decrees, blocked armies, and bloodied the palace—yet still flew letters to recruit crowds and reward villains, betraying ancestors above and cutting off the myriad hopes below.
translations.idiomatic: The dowager abetted him; when crime surfaced she resisted orders, armed her faction, and stained the palace—yet still shot appeals to arm traitors, dishonoring spirits and people.

sentences.zh: 昔文姜與亂，春秋所貶，呂宗叛戾，高后降配，宜廢皇太后為峻陽庶人。」

translations.literal: Formerly Wen Jiang joined turmoil—the Spring and Autumn demoted her; the Lü clan rebelled and Empress Gao was lowered in pairing. She should be demoted from empress dowager to commoner of Junyang.”
translations.idiomatic: Like Wen Jiang or Empress Lü, she must be struck from dowager rank and made a commoner of Junyang.”

sentences.zh: 中書監張華等以為「太后非得罪于先帝者也，今黨惡所親，[3]為不母于聖世。

translations.literal: Palace Supervisor Zhang Hua and others held: “The dowager did not offend the late emperor; now she joins wicked kin—she fails motherhood toward this sage age [3].
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua argued: “She never wronged Emperor Wu; siding with villains now breaks maternal duty in our era [3].

sentences.zh: 宜依孝成趙皇后故事，曰武帝皇后，處之離宮，以全貴終之恩。」

translations.literal: She should follow Empress Zhao of Emperor Cheng’s precedent—styled Empress of Emperor Wu and housed in a detached palace to preserve honored kindness to the end.”
translations.idiomatic: Treat her like Chengdi’s Zhao—call her Emperor Wu’s consort, lodge her apart, yet grant a decent end.”

sentences.zh: 尚書令、下邳王晃等議曰：「皇太后與駿潛謀，欲危社稷，不可復奉承宗廟，配合先帝。

translations.literal: Minister Director Prince Kang of Xiapi Huan and others debated: “The empress dowager secretly plotted with Jun to overturn the state—she cannot again serve the temple or pair with the late emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Huang countered: “She conspired with Yang Jun—she cannot share Wu’s temple.

sentences.zh: 宜貶尊號，廢詣金墉城。」

translations.literal: Her honored title should be stripped and she banished to Metal-Walled Fortress.”
translations.idiomatic: Strip her titles and lock her in Jinyong.”

sentences.zh: 于是有司奏：「請從晃等議，廢太后為庶人。

translations.literal: Thereupon the offices petitioned: “We ask following Huang’s proposal—depose the dowager as commoner.
translations.idiomatic: Officials petitioned: "We ask to adopt Huang's proposal and depose the dowager as a commoner.

sentences.zh: 遣使者以太牢告于郊廟，以奉承祖宗之命，稱萬國之望。

translations.literal: Dispatch envoys with grand sacrifice to announce at suburban altars and ancestral temple, obeying ancestor spirits and answering myriad lands’ expectation.
translations.idiomatic: Announce it with suburban bull sacrifice to ancestors and satisfy the realm.

sentences.zh: 至於諸所供奉，可順聖恩，務從豐厚。」

translations.literal: As for all provisions supplied, follow sagely kindness and strive for abundance.”
translations.idiomatic: Let her maintenance stay generous per your mercy.”

sentences.zh: 詔不許。

translations.literal: The edict did not permit.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 有司又固請，乃可之。

translations.literal: The offices pressed again; then he consented.
translations.idiomatic: They insisted again; he yielded.

sentences.zh: 又奏：「楊駿造亂，家屬應誅，詔原其妻龐命，以慰太后之心。

translations.literal: They also memorialized: “Yang Jun raised rebellion—his kin deserve execution; the edict spared his wife Pang to console the dowager.
translations.idiomatic: They added: “Yang Jun’s clan should die; you spared Lady Pang to comfort the dowager.

sentences.zh: 今太后廢為庶人，請以龐付廷尉行刑。」

translations.literal: Now that the dowager is demoted to commoner, we ask that Pang be handed to the Commandant of Justice for execution.”
translations.idiomatic: Now that she is a commoner, execute Lady Pang.”

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「聽龐與庶人相隨。」

translations.literal: The edict said: “Let Pang follow the commoner.”
translations.idiomatic: He ruled: “Let Lady Pang stay with her.”

sentences.zh: 有司希賈后旨，固請，乃從之。

translations.literal: The offices, courting Empress Jia’s intent, pressed firmly; then he followed.
translations.idiomatic: Bowing to Jia’s will they insisted until he agreed.

sentences.zh: 龐臨刑，太后抱持號叫，截髮稽顙，上表詣賈后稱妾，請全母命，不見省。

translations.literal: When Pang faced execution, the empress dowager clutched her, wailing; she cut her hair and knocked her forehead, submitted a memorial as concubine to Empress Jia begging to save her mother’s life—she was not granted audience.
translations.idiomatic: At Lady Pang’s execution the dowager clung to her, cut her hair, kowtowed, signed herself Jia’s servant to beg for mercy—Jia ignored her.

sentences.zh: 初，太后尚有侍御十餘人，賈后奪之，絕膳而崩，時年三十四，在位十五年。

translations.literal: At first the dowager still had more than ten attendants; Empress Jia seized them; she starved and died, aged thirty-four, having held rank fifteen years.
translations.idiomatic: Jia stripped her servants; she starved at thirty-four after fifteen years as consort.

sentences.zh: 賈后又信妖巫，謂太后必訴冤先帝，乃覆而殯之，施諸厭劾符書藥物。

translations.literal: Empress Jia further trusted witchcraft, fearing the dowager would appeal her grievance to the late emperor; she therefore buried her face-down with curse charms and drugs.
translations.idiomatic: Jia feared her ghost would accuse Emperor Wu, so she buried her prone under talismans.

sentences.zh: 永嘉元年，追復尊號，別立廟，神主不配武帝。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongjia her honored title was restored, a separate temple was established, and her spirit tablet was not paired with Emperor Wu.
translations.idiomatic: In 307 her title was restored, a separate shrine was built, and her tablet was not enshrined with Emperor Wu.

sentences.zh: 至成帝咸康七年，下詔使內外詳議。

translations.literal: By the seventh year of Xiankang under Emperor Cheng, an edict ordered inner and outer officials to debate the matter in detail.
translations.idiomatic: In 341 Emperor Cheng ordered court and capital officials to deliberate the question fully.

sentences.zh: 衛將軍虞潭議曰：世祖武皇帝光有四海，元皇后應乾作配。

translations.literal: Guards General Yu Tan argued: “Shizu Emperor Wu glorified the four seas; his primal empress matched Heaven’s pivot.”
translations.idiomatic: Guards General Yu Tan argued: “Emperor Wu illumined the realm; his first empress answered Heaven.”

sentences.zh: 元后既崩，悼后繼作，至楊駿肆逆，禍延天母。

translations.literal: After the primal empress died, the mourned empress succeeded; when Yang Jun ran riot, calamity reached the Mother of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: After Yang Yan died came Yang Zhi; Yang Jun’s treason dragged down the queen mother.

sentences.zh: 孝懷皇帝追復號諡，豈不以鯀殛禹興，義在不替者乎！

translations.literal: Emperor Huai restored her title and epithet—is this not because Gun was executed yet Yu rose—the principle of unbroken obligation?
translations.idiomatic: Huai restored her honors—as Gun fell but Yu rose, duty survives.

sentences.zh: 又太寧二年，臣忝宗正，帝譜泯棄，罔所循按。

translations.literal: Moreover in the second Taining year I humbly served as Director of the Imperial Clan; imperial genealogies were lost—nothing to consult.
translations.idiomatic: In Taining 316 I held the clan office; registers were gone.

sentences.zh: 時博諮舊齒，以定昭穆，與故驃騎將軍華恒、尚書荀崧、侍中荀邃因舊譜參論撰次，尊號之重，一無改替。

translations.literal: We broadly queried elders to fix generations and, with former General of Agile Cavalry Hua Heng, Minister Xun Song, Palace Attendant Xun Sui, reviewed old lists to compile order—her lofty title stayed unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: With Hua Heng, Xun Song, and Xun Sui we recomposed charts—her rank stood firm.

sentences.zh: 今聖上孝思，祗肅禋祀，詢及群司，將以恢定大禮。

translations.literal: Now our sage sovereign’s filial care solemnly tends sacrifice; he asks all bureaus to settle great ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Today’s ruler seeks your counsel to fix court ritual.

sentences.zh: 臣輒思詳，伏見惠皇帝起居注、群臣議奏，列駿作逆謀，危社稷，引魯之文姜，漢之呂后。

translations.literal: I have reflected carefully: in Emperor Hui’s daily records and ministers’ memorials they listed Jun’s treason, imperiling altars, citing Lu’s Wen Jiang and Han’s Empress Lü.
translations.idiomatic: Hui’s archives cite Wen Jiang and Empress Lü against Yang Jun.

sentences.zh: 臣竊以文姜雖莊公之母，實為父讎；

translations.literal: I quietly note that although Wen Jiang was Duke Zhuang’s mother, she was truly her husband’s foe;
translations.idiomatic: Wen Jiang was Duke Huan’s killer despite bearing Zhuang—

sentences.zh: 呂后寵樹私戚，幾危劉氏，按此二事異于今日。

translations.literal: Empress Lü favored kin until she nearly ended the Liu house—these two cases differ from today.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Lü nearly ruined Han—these differ from Yang Zhi.

sentences.zh: 昔漢章帝竇后殺和帝之母，和帝即位盡誅諸竇。

translations.literal: Formerly Dou empress of Han Zhangdi killed Emperor He’s mother; when He ascended he slaughtered the Dou clan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangdi’s Dou killed He’s mother; He wiped out the Dous.

sentences.zh: 當時議者欲貶竇后，及后之亡，欲不以禮葬。

translations.literal: Debates then wished to demote Dou empress; when she died some wished denial of ritual burial.
translations.idiomatic: Critics then sought to shame Dou and withhold burial rites.

sentences.zh: 和帝以奉事十年，義不可違，臣子之道，務從豐厚，仁明之稱，表于往代。

translations.literal: He had served her ten years—duty forbade cruelty; ministers pursued lavish burial—his humanity shone for ages.
translations.idiomatic: He refused cruelty after ten years’ care—his mercy became legend.

sentences.zh: 又見故尚書僕射裴頠議悼后故事，稱繼母雖出，追服無改。

translations.literal: I also saw former Minister Director Pei Yi’s opinion on Empress Dao’s case—though a stepmother had departed, mourning obligations stayed unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yi argued Emperor Ai’s mourned empress kept mourning even after divorce.

sentences.zh: 是以孝懷皇帝尊崇號諡，還葬峻陵。

translations.literal: Therefore Emperor Huai restored honored title and epithet and reburied her at Jun Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: So Huai restored her posthumous honors at Junling.

sentences.zh: 此則母子道全，而廢事蕩革也。

translations.literal: Thus mother-son duty stayed whole while violent deeds were swept away.
translations.idiomatic: Kin duty survived though politics had fouled them.

sentences.zh: 于時祭于弘訓之宮，未入太廟。

translations.literal: At that time sacrifice occurred at Hongxun Palace—not yet entering the great temple.
translations.idiomatic: She received offerings only at Hongxun, not the grand temple.

sentences.zh: 蓋是事之未盡，非義典也。

translations.literal: That was because the matter was unfinished—not canonical meaning.
translations.idiomatic: That showed work unfinished, not proper liturgy.

sentences.zh: 若以悼后復位為宜，則應配食世祖；

translations.literal: If restoring Empress Dao is right, she should share Emperor Wu’s offerings;
translations.idiomatic: If Yang Zhi deserves restoration, she must join Wu’s temple;

sentences.zh: 若以復之為非，則譜諡宜闕，未有位號居正，而偏祠別室者也。

translations.literal: if restoring her is wrong, then genealogies and epithets should lapse—one cannot hold orthodox rank yet dwell in a side shrine alone.
translations.idiomatic: if not, her titles should lapse—no legitimate rank receives only a side altar.

sentences.zh: 若以孝懷皇帝私隆母子之道，特為立廟者，此苟崇私情，有虧國典，則國譜帝諱，皆宜除棄，匪徒不得同祀于世祖之廟也。

translations.literal: If Emperor Huai privately enlarged mother-son feeling and built a special temple, that would exalt private affection yet wound state canon—then clan registers and temple names should all be discarded, not merely barred from Wu’s temple.
translations.idiomatic: A private shrine for filial piety alone would break precedent and void every register.

sentences.zh: 會稽王昱、中書監庾冰、中書令何充、尚書令諸葛恢、尚書謝廣、光祿勳留擢、丹楊尹殷融、護軍將軍馮懷、散騎常侍鄧逸等咸從潭議，由是太后配食武帝。

translations.literal: Prince Hui of Kuaiji Yu, Palace Supervisor Yu Bing, Palace Director He Chong, Minister Director Zhuge Hui, Minister Xie Guang, Superintendent of the Household Liu Zhuo, Intendant of Danyang Yin Rong, Defender-general Feng Huai, and Palace Rider Deng Yi all followed Tan’s opinion; thereby the dowager shared Emperor Wu’s sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yi, Yu Bing, He Chong, Zhuge Hui, Xie Guang, Liu Zhuo, Yin Rong, Feng Huai, and Deng Yi endorsed Tan—Yang Zhi joined Wu’s temple.

sentences.zh: 昔伯瑜之婉孌兮，每綵衣以娛親。

translations.literal: Ancient Boyu was tender—he often donned colored robes to cheer his parents.
translations.idiomatic: Like Boyu of Zhou I ache—he wore bright robes to delight his kin.

sentences.zh: 悼今日之乖隔兮，奄與家為參辰。

translations.literal: I mourn today’s cruel separation—suddenly with family I am Orion and Sirius.
translations.idiomatic: Today’s cruel divide casts kin as stars that never meet.

sentences.zh: 豈相去之云遠兮，曾不盈乎數尋。

translations.literal: How can they say the distance is far—it does not fill a few yards’ span.
translations.idiomatic: We stand mere feet apart yet cannot bridge the gap.

sentences.zh: 何宮禁之清切兮，欲瞻睹而莫因。

translations.literal: How sternly clear are palace barriers—I long to gaze yet find no way.
translations.idiomatic: Palace gates cut sharply—no path opens for my gaze.

sentences.zh: 仰行雲以歔欷兮，涕流射而沾巾。

translations.literal: I lift my eyes to drifting clouds and sigh; tears jet forth soaking my kerchief.
translations.idiomatic: I gaze at clouds and weep; tears stream until my sleeves drip.

sentences.zh: 惟屈原之哀感兮，嗟悲傷于離別。

translations.literal: Only Qu Yuan’s sorrow moves—alas for parting’s grief.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Yuan knew this ache—parting tears fall anew.

sentences.zh: 彼城闕之作詩兮，亦以日而喻月。

translations.literal: Those who made poems at the gate tower likewise paired sun with moon.
translations.idiomatic: The poets at the gate tower likened sun and moon—

sentences.zh: 況骨肉之相於兮，永緬邈而兩絕。

translations.literal: How much more flesh and bone sharing breath—forever distant, severed both ways.
translations.idiomatic: —yet kinship binds tighter than sun and moon, now lost forever.

sentences.zh: 長含哀而抱戚兮，仰蒼天而泣血。

translations.literal: Long bearing sorrow with clasped grief—I lift blue Heaven and weep blood.
translations.idiomatic: Endless sorrow grips me; I lift my eyes to Heaven and weep blood.

sentences.zh: 惟泰始十年秋七月丙寅，晉元皇后楊氏崩，嗚呼哀哉！

translations.literal: On the bingyin day of autumn in the seventh month of the tenth Taishi year the Jin primal empress Lady Yang died—alas!
translations.idiomatic: On that summer day in 274 Jin’s Empress Yang Yan passed—alas!

sentences.zh: 昔有莘適殷，姜姒歸周，宣德中闈，徽音永流。

translations.literal: Ancient Youxin married Yin; Jiang Si returned to Zhou—virtue spread within the palace, fair fame forever flows.
translations.idiomatic: Youxin wed Yin; Jiang water wed Zhou—inner chambers rang with virtue.

sentences.zh: 樊衛二姬，匡齊翼楚；

translations.literal: The two Ji ladies of Fan and Wei steadied Qi and aided Chu;
translations.idiomatic: Fan Ji and Wei Ji uplifted Qi and Chu;

sentences.zh: 馬鄧兩妃，亦毗漢主。

translations.literal: the two consorts Ma and Deng likewise aided Han sovereigns.
translations.idiomatic: Ma and Deng consorts beside Han sovereigns did the same.

sentences.zh: 峨峨元后，光嬪晉宇。

translations.literal: Lofty primal queen—you glorified consorts of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Towering primal queen—you lit the Jin harem.

sentences.zh: 伉儷聖皇，比蹤往古。

translations.literal: You matched the sage emperor—tracks aligned with ancient models.
translations.idiomatic: You walked beside the sage throne as queens of old.

sentences.zh: 遭命不永，背陽即陰。

translations.literal: Heaven granted no long span—you turned from yang toward shade.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven refused long life—you crossed from light to shade.

sentences.zh: 六宮號咷，四海慟心。

translations.literal: Six palaces wailed; four seas shared torn hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Six wings of the harem keened; all beneath Heaven tore their breasts.

sentences.zh: 嗟余鄙妾，銜恩特深。

translations.literal: Alas, mean concubine—I bore uniquely deep grace.
translations.idiomatic: Mean concubine though I am—your kindness pierced deepest.

sentences.zh: 追慕三良，甘心自沈。

translations.literal: I chase the Three Worthies—gladly I would sink myself.
translations.idiomatic: I envy the three who followed Duke Mu—I would gladly sink with you.

sentences.zh: 何用存思？

translations.literal: What use is longing?
translations.idiomatic: Why hoard longing?

sentences.zh: 不忘德音。

translations.literal: Never forget virtuous words.
translations.idiomatic: Keep your virtuous words alive.

sentences.zh: 何用紀述？

translations.literal: What use is chronicling?
translations.idiomatic: Why record deeds?

sentences.zh: 託辭翰林。

translations.literal: Entrust phrases to the brush grove.
translations.idiomatic: Commit them to ink and Hanlin.

sentences.zh: 乃作誄曰：

translations.literal: Thus she composed the dirge, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Thus runs her lament:

sentences.zh: 天祚貞吉，克昌克繁。

translations.literal: Heaven’s mandate stayed auspicious—multiplying, branching wide.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven kept auspicious fate—family branches multiplied.

sentences.zh: 則百斯慶，育聖育賢。

translations.literal: Thus came hundredfold blessing—bearing sages and worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Blessings arrived in hundreds—bearing sage sons and worthy princes.

sentences.zh: 教踰妊姒，訓邁姜嫄。

translations.literal: Teaching surpassed Ren and Si; instruction overtook Jiang Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Her teaching topped Si and Ren; her norms surpassed Jiang Yuan.

sentences.zh: 堂堂太子，惟國之元。

translations.literal: Grand stands the crown prince—root of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Lofty the heir—pillar of the realm.

sentences.zh: 濟濟南陽，為屏為藩。

translations.literal: Splendid princes of Nanyang—screens and hedges for the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Splendid Nanyang princes—screens and river guards.

sentences.zh: 本支菴藹，四海蔭焉。

translations.literal: Root and branch shade thick—four seas rest beneath.
translations.idiomatic: Root and branch spread shade—the realm rests cool.

sentences.zh: 微斯皇妣，孰茲克臻。

translations.literal: Without this royal mother—who could reach such zenith?
translations.idiomatic: Without this queen mother—who could climb so high?

sentences.zh: 曰乾蓋聰，曰聖允誠。

translations.literal: They say Qian is keen; they say sage is true.
translations.idiomatic: They call Heaven keen; they call sageness true.

sentences.zh: 積善之堂，五福所并。

translations.literal: Hall piled with goodness—five blessings assemble.
translations.idiomatic: Goodness piled high—the five blessings gather.

sentences.zh: 宜享高年，匪隕匪傾。

translations.literal: She should enjoy lofty years—not fall, not tilt.
translations.idiomatic: She deserved long years—never to fall or fail.

sentences.zh: 如彭之齒，如聃之齡。

translations.literal: Like Peng’s tooth-count; like Dan’s lifespan.
translations.idiomatic: Like Peng Zu’s span; like Laozi’s age.

sentences.zh: 云胡不造，于茲禍殃[5]。

translations.literal: Why was fortune not granted—here calamity struck [5]?
translations.idiomatic: Why deny Heaven’s favor—why strike her here [5]?

sentences.zh: 寢疾彌留，寤寐不康。

translations.literal: Illness lingered at death’s gate—sleep brought no peace.
translations.idiomatic: She lingered at death’s door—no sleep brought ease.

sentences.zh: 巫咸騁術，和鵲奏方。

translations.literal: Wu Xian wielded arts; He and Bian offered prescriptions.
translations.idiomatic: Shaman Wu worked spells; healers He and Que brewed drafts.

sentences.zh: 祈禱無應，嘗藥無良。

translations.literal: Prayers won no answer; tasted drugs brought no cure.
translations.idiomatic: Prayers failed; every draught proved vain.

sentences.zh: 形神將離，載昏載荒。

translations.literal: Body and spirit parted—darkening, wasting.
translations.idiomatic: Body and soul slipped apart—dimming into gloom.

sentences.zh: 奄忽崩殂，湮精滅光。

translations.literal: Suddenly she collapsed—spirit sank, light died.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly she fell—light drowned in dark.

sentences.zh: 哀哀太子，南陽繁昌。

translations.literal: Mournful crown prince—Nanyang’s flowering prince.
translations.idiomatic: The heir mourns—the flourishing prince of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 攀援不寐，擗踊摧傷。

translations.literal: He climbs yet cannot sleep—beats breast and breast is torn.
translations.idiomatic: He cannot climb from grief—beats his breast till bones break.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼哀哉！

translations.literal: Alas, oh grief!
translations.idiomatic: Alas for this sorrow!

sentences.zh: 闔宮號咷，宇內震驚。

translations.literal: Whole palace wailed—the realm within seas trembled.
translations.idiomatic: Every hall keened—the realm inside the seas shook.

sentences.zh: 奔者填衢，赴者塞庭。

translations.literal: Runners choked the avenues—mourners jammed the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: Runners clogged roads—mourners packed the yard.

sentences.zh: 哀慟雷駭，流淚雨零。

translations.literal: Grief crashed like thunder—tears fell like rain.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning crashed like thunder; tears fell like showers.

sentences.zh: 歔欷不已，若喪所生。

translations.literal: Sobs cease not—as if parents were lost.
translations.idiomatic: No sob ends—as if a parent died.

sentences.zh: 昔后之崩，大火西流。

translations.literal: When former queen died—great Fire constellation sank west.
translations.idiomatic: When she died last year—the Fire star slid west.

sentences.zh: 寒往暑過，今亦孟秋。

translations.literal: Cold went, heat passed—again we reach first autumn.
translations.idiomatic: Cold yielded to heat—again first autumn comes.

sentences.zh: 自我銜卹，儵忽一周。

translations.literal: Since I bore grief—a blur one full cycle.
translations.idiomatic: Since grief seized me—a year flashed past.

sentences.zh: 衣服將變，痛心若抽。

translations.literal: Garments soon change—pain grips like twisting entrails.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning clothes turn—my vitals twist.

sentences.zh: 逼彼禮制，惟以增憂。

translations.literal: Forced by ritual codes—only grief increases.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual presses harder—only sorrow swells.

sentences.zh: 去此素衣，結戀靈丘。

translations.literal: Leaving these plain robes—I cling to spirit hill.
translations.idiomatic: I shed white hemp yet cling to her burial mound.

sentences.zh: 有始有終，天地之經。

translations.literal: Having beginning and end—is Heaven and Earth’s warp.
translations.idiomatic: Beginnings and endings weave Heaven’s law.

sentences.zh: 自非三光，誰能不零。

translations.literal: Unless you are three luminaries—who avoids decay?
translations.idiomatic: Unless you are sun, moon, stars—who escapes falling?

sentences.zh: 存播令德，沒圖丹青。

translations.literal: Living she spread fair virtue—dead her image paints silks.
translations.idiomatic: Alive she spread virtue—dead artists paint her face.

sentences.zh: 先哲之志，以此為榮。

translations.literal: Former sages held this—their glory.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient worthies deemed this their glory.

sentences.zh: 溫溫元后，實宣慈焉。

translations.literal: Gentle primal queen—she truly spread kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Gentle primal queen—she widowed kindness.

sentences.zh: 撫育群生，恩惠滋焉。

translations.literal: She nurtured all creatures—grace welled forth.
translations.idiomatic: She nurtured every life—kindness overflowed.

sentences.zh: 遺愛不已，永見思焉。

translations.literal: Love left behind never ends—forever remembered.
translations.idiomatic: Her love lingers—memory never fades.

sentences.zh: 懸名日月，垂萬春焉。

translations.literal: Her name hangs with sun and moon—through myriad springs.
translations.idiomatic: Her name rides moon and sun—through endless springs.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼庶妾，感四時焉。

translations.literal: Alas mean concubine—I feel the four seasons.
translations.idiomatic: Mean concubine feels—four seasons turn.

sentences.zh: 言思言慕，涕漣洏焉。

translations.literal: Speaking longing, speaking yearning—tears trail down.
translations.idiomatic: Each word of longing—tears trail.

sentences.zh: 泰始九年，帝多簡良家子女以充內職，自擇其美者以絳紗繫臂。

translations.literal: In ninth Taishi year the emperor broadly drafted daughters of good houses for inner service and personally tied crimson gauze on those he deemed fairest.
translations.idiomatic: In 273 he drafted palace girls from good families and marked his favorites with crimson silk arm-bands.

sentences.zh: 而芳既入選，下殿號泣。

translations.literal: When Fang entered selection she descended the hall weeping and crying.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Fang crossed the hall weeping once chosen.

sentences.zh: 左右止之曰：「陛下聞聲。」

translations.literal: Attendants beside her stopped her: “His Majesty will hear your voice.”
translations.idiomatic: Attendants hissed, “The emperor will hear.”

sentences.zh: 芳曰：「死且不畏，何畏陛下！」

translations.literal: Fang said: “I fear not death—why fear His Majesty!”
translations.idiomatic: She shot back, “I fear death itself—why fear an emperor?”

sentences.zh: 帝遣洛陽令司馬肇策拜芳為貴嬪。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Luoyang Magistrate Sima Zhao to invest Fang as honorable lady by tally.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu had Luoyang prefect Sima Zhao invest her with honorable rank.

sentences.zh: 帝每有顧問，不飾言辭，率爾而答，進退方雅。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor questioned her she did not polish phrases—answered plainly yet withdrew with modest grace.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he questioned her she answered straight without flourish—yet comported herself with modest grace.

sentences.zh: 時帝多內寵，平吳之後復納孫皓宮人數千，自此掖庭殆將萬人。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor greatly favored inner chambers; after conquering Wu he took several thousand of Sun Hao’s palace women—thereafter pepper chambers neared ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: After Wu fell he absorbed thousands of Sun Hao’s girls until the harem neared ten thousand souls.

sentences.zh: 而並寵者甚眾，帝莫知所適，常乘羊車，恣其所之，至便宴寢。

translations.literal: Many equally favored—emperor knew not whom to choose—often rode goat-drawn cart wherever it pleased, feasting and bedding where it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: So many favorites he rode a goat cart wherever chance led and slept there.

sentences.zh: 宮人乃取竹葉插戶，以鹽汁灑地，而引帝車。

translations.literal: Palace ladies therefore inserted bamboo leaves in doors, sprinkled salt water on ground to lure emperor’s cart.
translations.idiomatic: Women sprinkled salt and hung bamboo leaves to steer his goat cart.

sentences.zh: 然芳最蒙愛幸，殆有專房之寵焉，侍御服飾亞于皇后。

translations.literal: Yet Fang received deepest favor—almost exclusive chamber privilege—attendants’ robes secondary only to empress.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Fang won nearest monopoly favor—her wardrobe rivaled the empress.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗與之摴蒱，爭矢，遂傷上指。

translations.literal: Emperor once played chupu with her; quarreling over arrows they wounded his finger.
translations.idiomatic: Playing dice for arrows she wounded his finger.

sentences.zh: 帝怒曰：「此固將種也！」

translations.literal: Emperor angrily said: “This truly is general stock!”
translations.idiomatic: He snapped, “That’s pure warrior blood!”

sentences.zh: 芳對曰：「北伐公孫，西距諸葛，非將種而何？」

translations.literal: Fang replied: “North you attacked Gongsun—west you resisted Zhuge—if not general stock, what?”
translations.idiomatic: She shot back, “You marched north against Gongsun and west against Zhuge—what else is warlord stock?”

sentences.zh: 帝甚有慚色。

translations.literal: The emperor felt deeply ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: He flushed with shame.

sentences.zh: 芳生武安公主。

translations.literal: Fang bore Princess Wu’an.
translations.idiomatic: She bore Princess Wu’an.

sentences.zh: 惠賈皇后諱南風，平陽人也，小名時。

translations.literal: Empress Jia of Hui, taboo Nanfeng, native of Pingyang, childhood name Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Jia Nanfeng of Pingyang—pet name Shi.

sentences.zh: 父充，別有傳。

translations.literal: Her father Chong has separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Jia Chong has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 初，武帝欲為太子取衛瓘女，元后納賈郭親黨之說，欲婚賈氏。

translations.literal: At first Emperor Wu wished crown prince to marry Wei Guan’s daughter; Empress Yuan listened to Jia and Guo faction urging marriage with Jia clan.
translations.idiomatic: Wu favored Wei Guan’s daughter; Empress Yang Yan pushed Jia kin.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「衛公女有五可，賈公女有五不可。

translations.literal: Emperor said: “Lord Wei’s daughter has five goods—Lord Jia’s daughter five bads.
translations.idiomatic: Wu said, “Wei’s girl scores five merits—Jia’s five flaws.

sentences.zh: 衛家種賢而多子，美而長白；

translations.literal: Wei house breeds wise and many sons—beautiful, tall, fair;
translations.idiomatic: Weis are fertile and wise—fair and statuesque;

sentences.zh: 賈家種妒而少子，醜而短黑。」

translations.literal: Jia house breeds jealousy and few sons—ugly, short, dark.”
translations.idiomatic: Jias are jealous and barren—dark and squat."

sentences.zh: 元后固請，荀顗、荀勖並稱充女之賢，乃定婚。

translations.literal: Empress Yuan pressed firmly—Xun Yi and Xun Xu together praised Chong’s daughter’s virtue—betrothal fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yan insisted; Xun Yi and Xun Xu praised Jia’s girl—the match closed.

sentences.zh: 始欲聘后妹午，午年十二，小太子一歲，短小未勝衣。

translations.literal: At first they wished to engage younger sister Wu—Wu twelve years old, one year younger than crown prince, too short for robes.
translations.idiomatic: They first chose sister Wu—twelve, petite beside the heir.

sentences.zh: 更娶南風，時年十五，大太子二歲。

translations.literal: They switched to Nanfeng—then fifteen, two years elder than crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: They wed Nanfeng instead—fifteen, two years his senior.

sentences.zh: 泰始八年二月辛卯[7]，冊拜太子妃。

translations.literal: Eighth Taishi year second month xinmao [7]—invested crown princess.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao in early 272 she became crown princess [7].

sentences.zh: 妒忌多權詐，太子畏而惑之，嬪御罕有進幸者。

translations.literal: Jealous, crafty in intrigue—crown prince feared yet dazed—concubines rarely gained favor.
translations.idiomatic: Jealous and scheming, she cowed the befuddled prince—other women seldom touched him.

sentences.zh: 后暴戾日甚。

translations.literal: Consort violent cruelty daily worsened.
translations.idiomatic: Her cruelty mounted daily.

sentences.zh: 侍中賈模，后之族兄，右衛郭彰，后之從舅，並以才望居位，與楚王瑋、東安公繇分掌朝政。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Jia Mo—consort’s lineage elder; Guards-general Guo Zhang—consort’s maternal uncle—both by talent and prestige held posts sharing governance with Prince Chu Wei and Duke Dongan Yao.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Mo and Guo Zhang ran court beside Sima Wei and Sima Yao.

sentences.zh: 后母廣城君養孫賈謐干預國事，權侔人主。

translations.literal: Consort mother Lady Guangcheng raised grandson Jia Mi meddling state affairs—authority matched sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Guo raised Jia Mi—his power rivaled the throne.

sentences.zh: 繇密欲廢后，賈氏憚之。

translations.literal: Yao secretly wished depose consort—Jia faction feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yao plotted deposition—Jias feared him.

sentences.zh: 及太宰亮、衛瓘等表繇徙帶方，奪楚王中候，后知瑋怨之，乃使帝作密詔令瑋誅瓘、亮，以報宿憾。

translations.literal: When Grand Mentor Liang and Wei Guan memorialized to exile Yao to Daifang and strip Prince Chu of central army inspector—consort knew Wei bore grudge—had emperor forge secret edict ordering Wei to kill Guan and Liang—settling old hatred.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Liang and Wei Guan banished Yao and clipped Wei’s guard—she forged orders for Sima Wei to murder Liang and Wei.

sentences.zh: 模知后凶暴，恐禍及己，乃與裴頠、王衍謀廢之，衍悔而謀寢。

translations.literal: Mo knew consort fierce—feared disaster reaching himself—with Pei Yi and Wang Yan plotted deposition—Yan repented—plot slept.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Mo saw danger—planned coup with Pei Yi—Wang Yan backed out.

sentences.zh: 初，后詐有身，內稿物為產具，遂取妹夫韓壽子慰祖養之，託諒闇所生，故弗顯。

translations.literal: At first consort feigned pregnancy—packed straw goods as birthing gear—then took sister’s husband Han Shou’s son Weizu raising—claimed mourning-hall birth—therefore not openly shown.
translations.idiomatic: She faked pregnancy—snatched Han Shou’s son Weizu—called him newborn heir.

sentences.zh: 遂謀廢太子，以所養代立。

translations.literal: Then plotted depose crown prince—establish fosterling.
translations.idiomatic: She meant to replace the heir with him.

sentences.zh: 時洛中謠曰：「南風烈烈吹黃沙，遙望魯國鬱嵯峨，前至三月滅汝家。」

translations.literal: Then Luoyang rhyme said: "South wind fierce blows yellow sand—far gaze Lu kingdom towering—before third month ends your house."
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang sang: "Nanfeng blasts yellow dust—far off Lu towers loom—by the third moon your house will fall."

sentences.zh: 后母廣城君以后無子，甚敬重愍懷，每勸厲后，使加慈愛。

translations.literal: Consort mother Lady Guangcheng because consort lacked sons greatly revered Crown Prince Minhuai—often urged consort—made her add kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Guo prized Minhuai—begged Jia to cherish him.

sentences.zh: 賈謐恃貴驕縱，不能推崇太子，廣城君恒切責之。

translations.literal: Jia Mi relied on pride—could not honor crown prince—Lady Guangcheng constantly scolded.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Mi insulted the heir—Lady Guo scolded him.

sentences.zh: 及廣城君病篤，占術謂不宜封廣城，乃改封宜城。

translations.literal: When Lady Guangcheng gravely ill—divination said unsuitable enfeoff Guangcheng—thereupon changed enfeoff Yicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Ill diviners forbade “Guangcheng”—she became Princess Yicheng.

sentences.zh: 后出侍疾十餘日，太子常往宜城第，將醫出入，恂恂盡禮。

translations.literal: Consort attended illness ten-plus days—crown prince often visited Yicheng mansion—brought physicians—obedient exhaustive ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Minhuai nursed her mother—deferential.

sentences.zh: 宜城臨終執后手，令盡意于太子，言甚切至。

translations.literal: Yicheng dying grasped consort’s hand—ordered exhaust feeling toward crown prince—speech extremely earnest.
translations.idiomatic: She clasped Jia’s hand—beg her shield Minhuai.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「趙粲及午必亂汝事，我死後，勿復聽入，深憶吾言。」

translations.literal: Also said: “Zhao Can and Wu surely ruin your affairs—after I die—never hear them again—deeply remember my words.”
translations.idiomatic: She also said, "Zhao Can and Jia Wu will surely disrupt your affairs; after I die, do not admit them again—remember my words well."

sentences.zh: 后不能遵之，遂專制天下，威服內外。

translations.literal: Consort could not obey—thereupon monopolized realm—awe subdued inner and outer.
translations.idiomatic: Jia ignored—ruled alone.

sentences.zh: 更與粲、午專為姦謀，誣害太子，眾惡彰著。

translations.literal: Further with Can, Wu solely plotted wickedness—slandered harmed crown prince—crowds of evils manifest.
translations.idiomatic: She schemed with them against Minhuai.

sentences.zh: 初，誅楊駿及汝南王亮、太保衛瓘、楚王瑋等，皆臨機專斷，宦人董猛參預其事。

translations.literal: At first executing Yang Jun and Prince Runan Liang, Grand Tutor Wei Guan, Prince Chu Wei—all improvised executions—eunuch Dong Meng participated.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jun, Sima Liang, Wei Guan, Sima Wei died by her whim—with eunuch Dong Meng.

sentences.zh: 猛，武帝時為寺人監，侍東宮，得親信于后，預誅楊駿，封武安侯，猛三兄皆為亭侯，天下咸怨。

translations.literal: Meng—Wu-era Inner Palace Overseer—served Eastern Palace—won consort trust—participated executing Yang Jun—enfeoffed Marquis Wu’an—Meng three elder brothers all village marquis—all realm resented.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Meng gained titles—his brothers too—the realm cursed them.

sentences.zh: 及太子廢黜，趙王倫、孫秀等因眾怨謀欲廢后[8]。

translations.literal: When crown prince deposed—Prince Zhao Lun and Sun Xiu exploiting resentment plotted depose consort [8].
translations.idiomatic: Once Minhuai fell Sima Lun and Sun Xiu used hatred to target her [8].

sentences.zh: 后數遣宮婢微服於人間視聽，其謀頗泄。

translations.literal: Consort repeatedly sent palace maids plain clothes among folk spy listen—plot leaked somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: She spied on rumors—some leaked.

sentences.zh: 后甚懼，遂害太子，以絕眾望。

translations.literal: Consort greatly afraid—thereupon harmed crown prince—cutting off hopes.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified she murdered Minhuai.

sentences.zh: 趙王倫乃率兵入宮，使翊軍校尉齊王冏入殿廢后。

translations.literal: Prince Zhao Lun then led troops palace—ordered Colonel Qi Wang Jiong enter hall depose consort.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Lun stormed in—sent Sima Jiong to drag her out.

sentences.zh: 后與冏母有隙，故倫使之。

translations.literal: Consort with Jiong’s mother bore grudge—therefore Lun sent him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong hated her mother—Lun used him.

sentences.zh: 后驚曰：「卿何為來！」

translations.literal: Consort alarmed said: “Why have you come!”
translations.idiomatic: She cried, “Why you!”

sentences.zh: 冏曰：「有詔收后。」

translations.literal: Jiong said: "There is an edict to seize you."
translations.idiomatic: Jiong said, "There is an edict to seize you."

sentences.zh: 后曰：「詔當從我出，何詔也？」

translations.literal: Consort said: "Edicts issue from me—what edict is this?"
translations.idiomatic: She snapped, "Edicts issue from me—what edict is this?"

sentences.zh: 后至上閤，遙呼帝曰：「陛下有婦，使人廢之，亦行自廢。」

translations.literal: Consort reaching upper chamber cried distant emperor: “Your Majesty has wife yet lets others depose her—you yourself will be deposed.”
translations.idiomatic: Reaching the upper chamber she cried to the emperor, "Your Majesty has a wife, yet you let others depose her—you will be deposed yourself."

sentences.zh: 又問冏曰：「起事者誰？」

translations.literal: Again asked Jiong: “Who raised revolt?”
translations.idiomatic: She asked Jiong again, "Who raised this affair?"

sentences.zh: 冏曰：「梁、趙。」

translations.literal: Jiong said: “Liang and Zhao.”
translations.idiomatic: “Liang and Zhao.”

sentences.zh: 后曰：「繫狗當繫頸，今反繫其尾，何得不然！」

translations.literal: Consort said: “Leash dog by throat—now leash tail—how can it not be so!”
translations.idiomatic: “Chain a dog by the throat—you seized the tail—no wonder!”

sentences.zh: 至宮西，見謐尸，再舉聲而哭遽止。

translations.literal: Reaching palace west saw Mi corpse—raised voice twice weeping suddenly stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Jia Mi’s corpse she wailed twice—then silence.

sentences.zh: 倫乃矯詔遣尚書劉弘等持節齎金屑酒賜后死。

translations.literal: Lun then forged edict dispatch Minister Liu Hong bearing tally deliver gold-filings wine grant consort death.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Lun sent Liu Hong with golden liquor.

sentences.zh: 后在位十一年。

translations.literal: Consort held rank eleven years.
translations.idiomatic: Eleven years queen.

sentences.zh: 趙粲、賈午、韓壽、董猛等皆伏誅。

translations.literal: Zhao Can, Jia Wu, Han Shou, Dong Meng executed.
translations.idiomatic: Her cabal died with her.

sentences.zh: 成都王穎伐長沙王乂，以討玄之為名。

translations.literal: Prince Chengdu Ying attacked Prince Changsha Yi—using punishing Xuanzhi as pretext.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Ying struck Sima Yi citing Yang Xuanzhi.

sentences.zh: 乂敗，穎奏廢后為庶人，處金墉城。

translations.literal: Yi defeated—Ying memorialized deposing consort as commoner—housed Metal-Walled Fortress.
translations.idiomatic: After Yi fell Ying reduced her to commoner at Jinyong.

sentences.zh: 陳眕等唱伐成都王，大赦，復后位。

translations.literal: Chen Zhen and others urged attacking Chengdu prince—grand amnesty—restored consort rank.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zhen’s coalition restored her with amnesty.

sentences.zh: 張方入洛，又廢后。

translations.literal: Zhang Fang entered Luoyang—again deposed consort.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fang returned and struck her title.

sentences.zh: 方逼遷大駕幸長安，留臺復后位。

translations.literal: Fang forced moving great carriage to Chang’an—Luoyang remnant court restored consort.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fang dragged the court west—Luoyang ministers restored her.

sentences.zh: 永興初，張方又廢后。

translations.literal: Early Yongxing—Zhang Fang again deposed consort.
translations.idiomatic: Early Yongxing Zhang Fang deposed her again.

sentences.zh: 河間王顒矯詔，以后屢為姦人所立，遣尚書田淑敕留臺賜后死。

translations.literal: Prince Hejian Yong forged edict—because consort repeatedly installed by villains—dispatched Minister Tian Shu ordering remnant court grant consort death.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yong forged orders—blaming meddlers—sent Tian Shu to kill her.

sentences.zh: 詔書累至，司隸校尉劉暾與尚書僕射荀藩、河南尹周馥馳上奏曰：「奉被手詔，伏讀惶悴。

translations.literal: Edicts piled—Metropolitan Commandant Liu Tun with Minister Director Xun Fan and Henan Intendant Zhou Fu galloped memorial saying: “Receiving handwritten edict—reading we tremble.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Tun, Xun Fan, and Zhou Fu raced a plea: “Your sealed orders leave us shaking.

sentences.zh: 臣按古今書籍，亡國破家，毀喪宗祊，皆由犯眾違人之所致也。

translations.literal: Your servants examine ancient and modern writings—states ruined, houses destroyed, ancestral temples smashed—all arise from offending masses and violating men.
translations.idiomatic: History shows ruin follows when rulers betray the people.

sentences.zh: 陛下遷幸，舊京廓然，眾庶悠悠，罔所依倚。

translations.literal: Your Majesty moved west—old capital empty—multitudes drift—nothing to lean on.
translations.idiomatic: You moved west—Luoyang lies bare—the people wander homeless.

sentences.zh: 家有跂踵之心，人想鑾輿之聲，思望大德，釋兵歸農。

translations.literal: Households feel standing-on-tiptoe hearts—people imagine carriage bells—longing for great virtue—lay down arms return farming.
translations.idiomatic: Every hearth cranes for your bells—the realm wants peace and fields.

sentences.zh: 而兵纏不解，處處互起，豈非善者不至，人情猜隔故耶！

translations.literal: Yet armies tangle unresolved—everywhere mutual rising—is it not because goodness has not arrived—human hearts suspiciously blocked?
translations.idiomatic: War still spreads because trust never came.

sentences.zh: 今上官巳犯闕稱兵，焚燒宮省，百姓諠駭，宜鎮之以靜。

translations.literal: Now Shangguan Si violates palace raising troops—burning palace offices—common folk clamor—should calm with stillness.
translations.idiomatic: Shangguan Si burns the palace—calm needs quiet rule.

sentences.zh: 而大使卒至，赫然執藥，當詣金墉，內外震動，謂非聖意。

translations.literal: Yet great envoy suddenly arrives—awefully clutching poison—about to reach Metal-Walled Fortress—inner and outer shaken—say this cannot be sagely intent.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly envoys bear poison for Jinyong—none believe it is your wish.

sentences.zh: 羊庶人門戶殘破，廢放空宮，門禁峻密，若絕天地，無緣得與姦人搆亂。

translations.literal: Lady Yang commoner gate shattered—cast aside empty palace—gate guards stern dense—as if heaven severed earth—no chance conspire with villains.
translations.idiomatic: Yang wallows locked away—no traitor access.

sentences.zh: 眾無智愚，皆謂不然，刑書猥至，罪不值辜，人心一憤，易致興動。

translations.literal: Crowds wise or foolish—none deem it right—punishment writs pile—crime does not match guilt—one surge of rage—easily stirs revolt.
translations.idiomatic: No one thinks her guilty—rash execution invites riot.

sentences.zh: 夫殺一人而天下喜悅者，宗廟社稷之福也。

translations.literal: To kill one yet realm rejoices—is fortune of ancestral temple altars.
translations.idiomatic: Execute one villain and the realm cheers—that aids the shrines.

sentences.zh: 今殺一枯窮之人而令天下傷慘，臣懼凶豎乘間，妄生變故。

translations.literal: Now kill one withered poor person yet order realm mourn—your servant fears vicious youths seize gap—recklessly breed change.
translations.idiomatic: Kill a helpless widow and horrify the realm—rebels will exploit it.

sentences.zh: 臣忝司京輦，觀察眾心，實以深憂，宜當含忍。

translations.literal: Your servant humbly supervises capital region—observing crowds’ hearts—truly deeply anxious—should tolerate endure.
translations.idiomatic: We guard the capital—we plead restraint.

sentences.zh: 不勝所見，謹密啟聞。

translations.literal: Unable bear what seen—respectfully secret memorial heard.
translations.idiomatic: We cannot stay silent.

sentences.zh: 願陛下更深與太宰參詳，勿令遠近疑惑，取謗天下。」

translations.literal: Wish Your Majesty deeper consult Grand Mentor—do not let far near doubt—invite slander realm-wide.”
translations.idiomatic: May Your Majesty consult further with the Grand Tutor in depth; do not let near and far grow doubtful and draw reproach from all under Heaven."

sentences.zh: 顒見表大怒，乃遣陳顏、呂朗東收暾。

translations.literal: Yong seeing memorial furious—thereupon dispatched Chen Yan and Lu Lang east seize Tun.
translations.idiomatic: Yong raged—sent Chen Yan and Lu Lang to arrest Liu Tun.

sentences.zh: 暾奔青州，后遂得免。

translations.literal: Tun fled Qingzhou—consort thereby escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Tun fled to Qingzhou—she survived.

sentences.zh: 帝還洛，迎后復位。

translations.literal: Emperor returned Luoyang—welcomed consort restored rank.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned he restored her.

sentences.zh: 後洛陽令何喬又廢后。

translations.literal: Later Luoyang Magistrate He Qiao again deposed consort.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate He Qiao struck her title again.

sentences.zh: 及張方首至，其日復后位。

translations.literal: When Zhang Fang’s head arrived—that day restored consort rank.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fang’s head reached Luoyang—she rose again that day.

sentences.zh: 會帝崩，后慮太弟立為嫂叔，不得稱太后，催前太子清河王覃入，將立之，不果。

translations.literal: Meeting emperor died—consort feared younger imperial brother enthroned would make aunt-and-uncle relation—unable title empress dowager—hurried former crown prince Qinghe prince Tan enter—about establish—did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: At Hui’s death she feared Sima Chi would make her sister-in-law—she rushed Tan—failed.

sentences.zh: 懷帝即位，尊后為惠帝皇后，居弘訓宮。

translations.literal: When Emperor Huai ascended—honored consort as Emperor Hui’s empress—dwelling Hongxun Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Huai styled her Hui’s widow at Hongxun.

sentences.zh: 洛陽敗，沒于劉曜。

translations.literal: Luoyang fell—submerged by Liu Yao.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang fell—Liu Yao seized her.

sentences.zh: 曜僭位，以為皇后。

translations.literal: Yao usurped throne—made her empress.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao made her consort.

sentences.zh: 因問曰：「吾何如司馬家兒？」

translations.literal: Therefore asked: “How compare to Sima house boy?”
translations.idiomatic: He asked, “How do I compare to that Sima?”

sentences.zh: 后曰：「胡可並言？

translations.literal: Consort said: “How may they be spoken together?
translations.idiomatic: She answered, “There is no comparison.

sentences.zh: 陛下開基之聖主，彼亡國之暗夫，有一婦一子及身三耳，不能庇之。

translations.literal: Your Majesty founding sacred lord—that defeated-house dull husband—with one wife one son and himself only three—could not shelter them.
translations.idiomatic: You are a founding hero—he could not shield wife, son, self.

sentences.zh: 貴為帝王，而妻子辱于凡庶之手。

translations.literal: Noble yet emperor—wife and children humiliated by common hands.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor though he was—kin suffered common abuse.

sentences.zh: 遣妾爾時實不思生，何圖復有今日。

translations.literal: Banished concubine then truly wished not live—how scheme again have today.
translations.idiomatic: I thought life over—never dreamed of this dawn.

sentences.zh: 妾生於高門，常謂世間男子皆然。

translations.literal: Concubine born high gate—always thought world’s men all thus.
translations.idiomatic: Raised noble—I assumed every man so weak.

sentences.zh: 自奉巾櫛以來，始知天下有丈夫耳。」

translations.literal: Since serving towel comb—begin know world has real husbands.”
translations.idiomatic: Since serving you with comb and towel, I have learned that the world truly has real men."

sentences.zh: 曜甚愛寵之，生曜二子而死，偽諡獻文皇后。

translations.literal: Yao greatly loved favored her—bore Yao two sons then died—false posthumous title Offered Culture Empress.
translations.idiomatic: He adored her—she bore two sons then died—honored posthumously as Empress Xianwen.

sentences.zh: 惠帝在東宮，將納妃。

translations.literal: When Emperor Hui in Eastern Palace—about to take consort.
translations.idiomatic: While Hui was heir they chose a princess.

sentences.zh: 武帝慮太子尚幼，未知帷房之事，乃遣往東宮侍寢，由是得幸有身。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu worried crown prince still young—did not know inner chamber affairs—therefor dispatched go Eastern Palace attend bedding—thereby gained favor pregnant.
translations.idiomatic: Wu sent her to tutor him in bed—she conceived.

sentences.zh: 賈后妒忌之，玖求還西宮，遂生愍懷太子，年三四歲，惠帝不知也。

translations.literal: Empress Jia jealous—Jiu begged return western palace—thereby bore Crown Prince Minhuai—age three four years—Emperor Hui did not know.
translations.idiomatic: Jia drove her west—she bore Minhuai—Hui knew nothing for years.

sentences.zh: 入朝，見愍懷與諸皇子共戲，執其手，武帝曰：「是汝兒也。」

translations.literal: Entering court seeing Minhuai playing with imperial sons—grasped his hand—Emperor Wu said: “This is your son.”
translations.idiomatic: Entering court and seeing Minhuai playing with the imperial sons, he took his hand and Emperor Wu said, "This is your son."

sentences.zh: 及立為太子，拜玖為淑媛。

translations.literal: When established crown prince—invested Jiu as Shuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Minhuai became heir she became Shuyuan.

sentences.zh: 賈后不聽太子與玖相見，處之一室。

translations.literal: Empress Jia did not permit crown prince meet Jiu—housed one chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Jia barred visits—penned mother and son apart.

sentences.zh: 及愍懷遇酷，玖亦被害焉。

translations.literal: When Minhuai met cruel fate—Jiu also murdered.
translations.idiomatic: When Minhuai died killers took her too.

sentences.zh: 永康初，詔改葬太子，因贈玖夫人印綬，葬顯平陵。

translations.literal: Early Yongkang—edict reburied crown prince—thereupon granted Jiu lady seals—buried Xianping Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: Yongkang reburied Minhuai—honored her at Xianping.
